{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"系统性地从分类学相关性过渡到分子机制，详细列举了多种微生物代谢物和蛋白质如何通过特定受体（GPCRs, A2AR, STING, NOD2, TLR5）和信号通路影响宿主免疫系统。","limits":"所给摘要未交代具体的文献检索策略和纳入排除标准；主要依赖已发表的小鼠模型和少量临床数据，缺乏大规模前瞻性干预试验的直接证据；对于非细菌类微生物（真菌、古菌）及抑制性微生物的关注不足。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"小鼠模型及患者队列中的相关性研究","finding":"特定细菌属（如双歧杆菌、拟杆菌、阿克曼氏菌、普拉梭菌）的存在与ICB疗效正相关，但不同研究间结果存在异质性，且相关性不等于因果性。"},{"conditions":"粪菌移植（FMT）和单菌定植实验","finding":"来自响应者的FMT可重现抗肿瘤效应，增加肿瘤内CD8+ T细胞浸润；特定菌株（如A. muciniphila, Bifidobacterium spp.）的单菌定植足以增强ICB疗效。"},{"conditions":"短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）的作用","finding":"SCFAs（如丁酸盐）对ICB的影响具有双重性：通常促进Treg和效应T细胞分化，但在某些情况下（如抗CTLA-4治疗）可能产生负面影响。"},{"conditions":"肌苷（Inosine）通路","finding":"B. pseudolongum等产生的肌苷通过结合T细胞上的A2AR受体，协同TLR9激动剂增强抗CTLA-4疗效，但单独使用不足以完全重现表型。"},{"conditions":"Akkermansia muciniphila与STING通路","finding":"A. muciniphila产生cdAMP，激活STING信号，诱导I型干扰素产生，招募NK细胞和树突状细胞，从而增强抗肿瘤免疫。"},{"conditions":"Enterococcus sagA蛋白与NOD2通路","finding":"肠球菌表达的SagA蛋白降解肽聚糖产生muropeptides，激活宿主NOD2受体，促进炎症环境和CD8+ T细胞浸润。"},{"conditions":"分子模拟机制","finding":"E. hirae中的噬菌体尾长测量蛋白（TMP）含有与宿主PSMB4蛋白相似的表位，引发交叉反应性CD8+ T细胞，增强抗PD-1疗效。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管已知特定微生物群与ICB疗效相关，但确切的分子机制尚不清楚，这限制了将微生物作为精准医疗手段加以利用的能力。本文试图回答：哪些具体的微生物分子特征（蛋白质、酶、代谢物）介导了这种调节作用？","research_scope":"人类微生物群（特别是肠道菌群）与癌症免疫治疗中免疫检查点阻断（ICB，如抗PD-1/PD-L1和抗CTLA-4抗体）疗效之间的关系。研究范围涵盖从宏观的菌群组成相关性到微观的分子机制（代谢物、蛋白质、抗原模拟），以及基于这些机制的工程化益生菌策略。"}

identity.title: Role of gut microbiome on immunotherapy efficacy in melanoma

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤免疫检查点抑制剂疗效”提供了关键的背景框架和具体菌属证据。它特别适用于回答微生物群组成与ICI疗效之间的相关性（Facet F1），以及部分介导机制（如T细胞激活、代谢产物作用）（Facet F2）。其价值在于提供了具体的微生物分类单元（Taxa）列表和临床前转化证据，但需注意其结论多为关联性而非因果确证，且临床干预证据尚不成熟。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该论文主要针对黑色素瘤，虽然提及肾癌和非小细胞肺癌，但核心证据集中在黑色素瘤。在将其结论推广到其他实体瘤时需格外谨慎。","文中提到的“机制”多为基于动物模型的推断或临床观察的相关性，不能直接等同于已确证的分子机制。","关于益生菌、益生元等干预措施的效果，文中明确指出“临床数据有限”或“仍在进行中”，不应将其视为已确立的治疗标准。","FMT的证据主要来自动物实验和少量早期临床试验，其长期安全性和有效性尚未完全确立。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"系统总结了肠道微生物群作为生物标志物预测黑色素瘤ICI疗效的具体菌属特征；整合了从基础机制到临床干预（特别是FMT）的多层次证据；明确了抗生素使用对ICI疗效的负面影响。","limits":"所引用的临床数据多基于小样本观察性研究或回顾性分析，缺乏大规模随机对照试验的支持；不同研究间的微生物测序方法和分析流程可能存在差异，导致结果难以直接比较；大部分干预性证据（如益生菌、FMT增强疗效）仍局限于动物模型或早期可行性研究，尚未确立标准化的治疗方案；对于非黑色素瘤实体瘤的外推需谨慎。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"临床前小鼠模型（Vetizou et al., Matson et al., Gopalakrishnan et al.）","finding":"无菌或抗生素处理的小鼠对抗CTLA-4或抗PD-1治疗产生耐药性；回植特定有益菌（如Bacteroides fragilis, Bifidobacterium spp.）或来自人类响应者的粪便微生物可恢复或增强抗肿瘤免疫反应。"},{"conditions":"黑色素瘤患者临床队列（Matson et al., Gopalakrishnan et al.）","finding":"响应者粪便中富集Bifidobacterium longum/adolescentis, Faecalibacterium, Ruminococcae等菌属；无响应者则富集Ruminococcus obeum, Roseburia intestinalis, Bacteroidales等。微生物特征与循环T细胞亚群比例相关。"},{"conditions":"抗生素使用与ICI疗效关联","finding":"在ICI治疗前后使用抗生素（尤其是广谱抗生素）与较差的临床预后和无响应率增加相关，提示抗生素引起的菌群失调可能削弱免疫治疗效果。"},{"conditions":"粪便微生物移植（FMT）","finding":"将响应者的粪便移植给黑色素瘤患者或小鼠模型显示出改善ICI疗效的潜力；同时FMT也被用于成功治疗ICI相关的结肠炎。多项针对黑色素瘤的FMT联合ICI临床试验正在进行中。"}],"problem_or_question":"肠道微生物群如何影响免疫检查点抑制剂的临床疗效？如何通过调节肠道微生物群来预测疗效、增强抗肿瘤反应或减轻免疫相关不良反应（如结肠炎）？","research_scope":"肠道微生物群（gut microbiome）在实体瘤免疫治疗中的作用，重点聚焦于黑色素瘤（melanoma），涉及免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）的疗效预测、不良反应管理及微生物群调节策略。"}

identity.title: Obesity, cancer, and response to immune checkpoint inhibitors: Could the gut microbiota be the mechanistic link?

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review is highly relevant for discussing the 'obesity paradox' in immunotherapy and the proposed role of the gut microbiota as a mechanistic bridge. It provides a comparative table of microbial taxa associated with obesity versus ICI response, which helps illustrate the complexity of the link (overlap vs. divergence). It also details specific metabolic and immune pathways (leptin, FASN, inflammation) that could mediate this interaction, offering mechanistic hypotheses for the planning of future empirical studies.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review is a narrative synthesis; do not treat its conclusions as definitive proof of causality.","The 'obesity paradox' findings are primarily from retrospective cohort studies and pooled analyses, subject to confounding.","Direct evidence linking the *obese* microbiome specifically to *ICI response* is acknowledged as scarce; much of the link is inferred from separate bodies of literature.","BMI is the primary metric discussed, but the authors note its limitations regarding body composition."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Provides a comprehensive conceptual framework linking obesity, gut microbiota, and ICI response, highlighting the 'obesity paradox' and proposing microbiota as a mediator.","limits":"The review is narrative and does not present original quantitative data. It acknowledges a lack of direct clinical trials that stratify patients by both BMI and microbiota status simultaneously. Mechanistic claims are largely based on correlational data or preclinical models, not confirmed causal pathways in humans."},{"contribution":"Identifies specific bacterial taxa (Akkermansia, Faecalibacterium, Bifidobacterium) with strong evidence for ICI response, while noting their complex relationship with obesity.","limits":"Microbiota analysis methods vary across cited studies (16S rRNA vs. metagenomics), making cross-study comparisons difficult. The review notes that current analyses often focus only on bacteria, ignoring fungi, viruses, and archaea."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"In observational cohorts of metastatic melanoma, NSCLC, and renal cell carcinoma treated with ICIs.","finding":"Obese patients (higher BMI) generally show improved overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) compared to normal-weight patients, creating an 'obesity paradox'. This effect is less pronounced or absent in chemotherapy-treated groups."},{"conditions":"Comparative analysis of microbiota profiles from published literature.","finding":"There is partial overlap but also significant discordance between microbiota enriched in obese patients and those enriched in ICI responders. For example, Lactobacillus and Bacteroides are enriched in both, whereas Akkermansia muciniphila and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii are enriched in ICI responders but not typically in obese patients (or are depleted)."},{"conditions":"Preclinical and mechanistic studies cited.","finding":"Obesity induces a pro-inflammatory state (elevated leptin, TNF-alpha, IL-6) and alters T-cell exhaustion markers (PD-1). Microbiota can modulate these pathways via short-chain fatty acids affecting leptin secretion or through direct immune cross-reactivity (e.g., Bifidobacterium stimulating CD8+ T cells)."}],"problem_or_question":"The review addresses why obese patients frequently exhibit improved responses to ICIs despite obesity historically being associated with poor cancer prognosis. It seeks to identify if and how the gut microbiota mediates this relationship, proposing it as a unifying mechanism for the observed clinical paradox.","research_scope":"The review focuses on the intersection of three domains: obesity (defined primarily by BMI, with discussion of visceral adiposity and body composition), solid tumors (specifically melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, colorectal, breast, and hepatocellular carcinomas), and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). It examines the biological and clinical interactions between these factors, with a specific emphasis on the gut microbiota as a potential mechanistic bridge."}

identity.title: [Tracking Research Progress in the Modulatory Role of Gut Microbiome in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors Applied in Cancer Treatment].

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为理解肠道微生物组如何调节ICIs疗效提供了结构化的证据框架，特别有助于区分不同ICIs类型（PD-1 vs CTLA-4 vs CD47）对应的不同菌群特征和机制路径。它提供了具体的菌属-效应关联列表、潜在的分子机制线索（STING、肌苷、Th1分化）以及临床转化（FMT/益生菌）的现状，适合作为综述中“机制”和“临床相关性”部分的素材来源。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述涵盖多种肿瘤类型（实体瘤和血液瘤），但在回答针对“solid tumours”的具体问题时，需注意区分不同癌种（如黑色素瘤、NSCLC、HCC）的证据强度，不能简单合并所有结果。","CTLA-4抑制剂与菌群的关系存在直接矛盾的证据（拟杆菌的作用），在综合时需明确指出这种不一致性，而非选择一个单一结论。","许多机制证据来自小鼠模型（如STING通路、肌苷作用），在应用于人类时需保持谨慎，明确标注为“动物模型证据”。","综述中提到的临床试验多为早期阶段或计划中，不能作为疗效已证实的依据，仅反映研究趋势。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"系统梳理了不同类别ICIs（PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4, CD47）与肠道微生物组的相互作用证据，区分了不同菌属在不同治疗背景下的正向或负向关联。","limits":"作为综述，其结论依赖于所引用的原始研究，本身不提供新的实验数据。文中指出当前领域存在方法学不统一、动物模型外推限制、个体基线差异大等问题，综述本身未解决这些根本性局限。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"PD-1/PD-L1抑制剂治疗（黑色素瘤、NSCLC、HCC等）","finding":"特定有益菌群（如双歧杆菌属、粪杆菌属、长双歧杆菌、乳酸杆菌等）的富集与更好的治疗反应（延长PFS/TTF、增加TILs、增强记忆T细胞/NK细胞活性）相关。机制涉及促进树突状细胞成熟、诱导IFN-γ产生、抑制病原体毒力因子等。"},{"conditions":"CTLA-4抑制剂治疗（黑色素瘤、肉瘤模型）","finding":"结果存在争议：部分研究显示拟杆菌属增多或口服拟杆菌补充剂可触发Th1反应、促进DC成熟从而增强疗效；另一项研究发现拟杆菌属过量表达削弱疗效，而粪杆菌属及厚壁菌门与更好疗效相关（可能通过诱导Treg失活）。抗生素使用通常降低疗效，阿克曼菌再定植可恢复PD-1阻断疗效。"},{"conditions":"CD47抑制剂治疗","finding":"肠道菌群是CD47阻断治疗生效的必要条件。双歧杆菌可通过激活STING信号通路（依赖I型干扰素信号），促进DC交叉提呈，从而增强CD47阻断剂的抗肿瘤作用。"},{"conditions":"代谢机制探索","finding":"Mager等发现长双歧杆菌产生的肌苷（嘌呤代谢物）可通过A2AR信号介导促进Th1细胞分化，增强CTLA-4和PD-L1抑制剂的疗效，提示微生物代谢产物是重要中介。"},{"conditions":"临床应用尝试","finding":"FMT和益生菌干预正在多项临床试验中进行评估，旨在通过调节菌群提高ICIs疗效或管理不良反应（如结肠炎风险预测）。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管免疫检查点抑制剂在多种癌症治疗中显示出巨大潜力，但患者应答率较低且存在异质性耐药和不良反应。肠道微生物组被认为在其中起关键调控作用，但其具体调控机制、对不同ICIs类型的特异性影响以及临床转化策略尚需系统梳理。","research_scope":"肠道微生物组在免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs，包括PD-1/PD-L1、CTLA-4、CD47抑制剂）治疗肿瘤过程中的调控作用。涵盖实体瘤（如黑色素瘤、非小细胞肺癌、肝细胞癌、肾细胞癌等）及血液系统恶性肿瘤，涉及临床前动物模型与人类临床试验证据。"}

identity.title: Gut microbiota reshaping the pancreatic cancer immune microenvironment: new avenues for immunotherapy

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤中免疫检查点抑制剂疗效”这一主题提供了详细的机制背景和多维度的证据素材。它不仅涵盖了PDAC这一特定实体瘤，还涉及了黑色素瘤等其他实体瘤的比较视角。重点在于提供微生物群影响ICI疗效的具体细胞机制（如DC激活、T细胞分化）、关键代谢物（SCFAs, TMAO）的作用路径，以及临床实践中菌群变化与治疗反应的关联实例。同时，它也提供了反面案例（如无效的临床组合），有助于全面评估微生物干预的复杂性。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述主要聚焦于胰腺癌，虽然引用了黑色素瘤等其他实体瘤的研究来佐证机制，但在应用于其他实体瘤时需考虑肿瘤特异性的差异。","许多机制结论基于小鼠模型，人类肠道菌群的个体差异极大，直接外推需谨慎。","临床数据多为回顾性或小型试验，缺乏大规模前瞻性随机对照试验的支持，特别是关于特定菌株对ICI疗效的确切因果影响。","作者提到的“Veillonella导致耐药”等观点基于特定研究，可能存在情境依赖性，不应视为普遍共识。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"系统总结了肠道微生物群调控PDAC免疫微环境的多种细胞类型和分子机制，特别是明确了不同菌群/代谢物对T细胞亚群（Th17/Treg, CD8+）的双向调节作用。","limits":"所给材料未交代具体的文献检索策略、纳入排除标准及质量评价方法。大部分证据来自小鼠模型，直接外推至人类的可靠性受限。"},{"contribution":"提供了微生物群作为预测ICI疗效生物标志物的潜在候选者列表（如Akkermansia, Veillonella）。","limits":"部分关联仅基于观察性研究或单一队列，缺乏大规模前瞻性验证。例如，Vancomycin联合Nivolumab的II期试验显示无临床获益，提示简单改变菌群未必能转化为临床成功。"},{"contribution":"提出了包括FMT、益生菌、饮食在内的多种微生物干预策略，并指出了标准化缺失的问题。","limits":"对于具体菌株的最佳剂量、给药途径及长期安全性缺乏统一结论。目前尚无针对PDAC的大规模随机对照临床试验证实这些策略的有效性。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"基于小鼠模型（如KC/KPC模型）及体外研究","finding":"肠道微生物群可通过TLR信号通路促进M2型巨噬细胞极化，建立免疫抑制性TME；而某些益生菌（如L. casei, L. reuteri）可抑制TLR4信号，促进M1型极化。"},{"conditions":"基于微生物代谢物分析","finding":"短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）如丁酸、戊酸可通过表观遗传修饰（HDAC抑制）增强CD8+ T细胞的抗肿瘤活性及CAR-T疗法效果；TMAO可重编程巨噬细胞以增强效应T细胞功能。"},{"conditions":"基于PDAC患者队列及动物模型","finding":"特定的微生物组成（如Akkermansia muciniphila, Bifidobacterium丰度高）与更好的ICI疗效相关；而Veillonella等特定菌属的富集可能与PD-1阻断治疗的耐药性及较差的生存期相关。"},{"conditions":"基于临床前试验","finding":"FMT或特定益生菌（如L. reuteri）在PDAC小鼠模型中能显著抑制肿瘤生长并增强NK细胞浸润。"}],"problem_or_question":"胰腺癌对传统免疫治疗反应不佳，亟需寻找改善预后的新途径。肠道微生物群作为重要的外部调节因子，其在PDAC免疫微环境重塑中的作用机制是什么？如何通过这些机制优化现有的免疫治疗策略？","research_scope":"胰腺导管腺癌（PDAC）；肠道微生物群及其代谢产物；肿瘤免疫微环境（TME）中的先天性和适应性免疫细胞；免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）、CAR-T疗法及微生物靶向干预策略。"}

identity.title: Effect of gut microbiota on immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) based cancer immunotherapy

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review serves as a foundational resource for understanding the biological plausibility and clinical evidence linking gut microbiota to ICI efficacy in solid tumors. It provides detailed mechanistic pathways (molecular mimicry, DC activation, metabolite signaling) and lists specific bacterial taxa associated with response or resistance. It also outlines practical strategies for microbiome modulation and identifies key controversies, making it useful for constructing the theoretical framework and discussing clinical translation challenges in the broader review.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review is a narrative synthesis, not a systematic review; it may not capture all recent studies or provide a balanced statistical summary of effect sizes.","Many mechanistic insights are extrapolated from mouse models, which may not fully replicate human gut microbiota complexity and immune responses.","Conflicting evidence exists within the cited literature (e.g., the role of Bacteroides), reflecting the heterogeneity of the field rather than a settled consensus.","The review highlights individual variability as a major challenge, implying that 'one-size-fits-all' microbial interventions are unlikely to be effective without personalization."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Provides a comprehensive overview of the mechanistic links between gut microbiota and ICI efficacy, categorizing beneficial and detrimental bacterial species across different cancer types and ICI targets.","limits":"As a narrative review, it does not present original experimental data or perform a systematic quantitative meta-analysis. The conclusions are based on the interpretation of diverse studies with varying methodologies."},{"contribution":"Highlights the clinical potential of microbiome-based biomarkers and therapeutic adjuncts (e.g., FMT, probiotics) for personalized cancer immunotherapy.","limits":"Acknowledges significant challenges including high inter-individual variability, lack of standardized protocols for microbiome analysis and intervention, and discrepancies between mouse model results and human clinical trials."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"In mouse models and human clinical studies of melanoma and other solid tumors treated with ICIs","finding":"Specific gut bacterial compositions are associated with differential responses to ICI therapy. Beneficial bacteria such as Bifidobacterium spp., Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Akkermansia muciniphila, and Ruminococcaceae are linked to improved response rates and survival, whereas Bacteroides spp. and certain other taxa are associated with resistance."},{"conditions":"Mechanistic analysis of immune modulation","finding":"Gut microbiota modulates ICI efficacy through multiple mechanisms: (1) molecular mimicry where bacterial antigens prime cross-reactive T cells; (2) activation of dendritic cells via microbial-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs); and (3) production of metabolites like short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that influence immune cell function and cytokine production."},{"conditions":"Clinical interventions involving microbiome modulation","finding":"Strategies such as FMT from responders to non-responders, administration of specific bacterial consortia, and dietary modifications have shown promise in restoring or enhancing ICI efficacy in preclinical and early clinical settings."}],"problem_or_question":"The review addresses the problem of primary and acquired resistance to ICI-based immunotherapy, which limits its clinical application. It seeks to understand the role of gut microbiota as a key factor affecting patient response heterogeneity and explores how modulating the gut microbiome can optimize therapeutic outcomes.","research_scope":"The review focuses on the interaction between human gut microbiota and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) based cancer immunotherapy, specifically targeting anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 therapies. It covers mechanisms of action, clinical evidence from mouse models and human studies, strategies for microbiome modulation, and challenges in application."}

identity.title: Facts and Hopes for Gut Microbiota Interventions in Cancer Immunotherapy

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review serves as a foundational resource for understanding the biological plausibility and clinical status of microbiome-immunotherapy interactions. It provides detailed mechanistic hypotheses (direct T-cell stimulation, mimicry, metabolites) and a critical assessment of why human biomarker discovery has been challenging (cohort heterogeneity). It also offers concrete examples of intervention strategies (FMT, consortia) and their preliminary clinical outcomes, which are essential for discussing the transition from association to causation and therapy.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review covers multiple solid tumor types (melanoma, NSCLC, RCC, GI cancers); findings may not be generalizable to hematologic malignancies or other cancer types not discussed.","Human data are primarily observational associations; causal claims should be attributed to preclinical models unless supported by interventional trial data.","Biomarker findings are inconsistent across studies; do not present any single taxon as a definitive universal predictor without noting the cohort-specific nature of the evidence.","Clinical trial results are from early phases; avoid overstating efficacy or safety based on small sample sizes."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Provides a comprehensive synthesis of preclinical and clinical evidence linking the gut microbiome to ICI efficacy and toxicity, categorizing mechanisms into three distinct themes.","limits":"As a narrative review, it does not perform a quantitative meta-analysis; it highlights the lack of consensus in human biomarker studies rather than resolving it."},{"contribution":"Critically evaluates the limitations of current human studies, including small sample sizes, geographic biases, and analytical pipeline differences, advocating for standardized large-scale datasets.","limits":"Does not provide definitive answers on which specific microbial signatures are universally predictive across all solid tumor types."},{"contribution":"Summarizes early-phase clinical trial data for various microbiome interventions (FMT, consortia, diet), offering a landscape of current therapeutic developments.","limits":"Most clinical trial data reported are from early-phase (I/II) studies with small sample sizes; long-term efficacy and safety profiles are not yet established."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"Preclinical mouse models","finding":"Specific commensals (e.g., Bifidobacterium spp., Akkermansia muciniphila, Bacteroides fragilis) enhance anti-PD-1 or anti-CTLA-4 efficacy via dendritic cell activation, STING pathway signaling, and modulation of T-cell subsets."},{"conditions":"Human observational studies (Melanoma, NSCLC, RCC)","finding":"Responders to ICIs often show higher abundance of specific taxa (e.g., Faecalibacterium, Ruminococcaceae, A. muciniphila), but there is no consensus on a universal predictive signature due to cohort-specific variations, geographic differences, and methodological heterogeneity."},{"conditions":"Antibiotic use during ICI therapy","finding":"Broad-spectrum antibiotic use is consistently associated with reduced progression-free survival and overall survival in ICI-treated patients, likely due to depletion of beneficial microbes."},{"conditions":"Mechanistic pathways","finding":"Three primary mechanisms are identified: (1) direct stimulation of antitumor T-cells; (2) molecular mimicry between bacterial and tumor antigens; (3) production of immunomodulatory metabolites like short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), secondary bile acids, and inosine."},{"conditions":"Immune-related adverse events (irAEs)","finding":"Specific microbiota profiles are linked to irAEs, particularly colitis. For example, certain Firmicutes are associated with anti-CTLA-4 colitis, and Streptococcus abundance correlates with arthritis and poor prognosis."},{"conditions":"Clinical trials of FMT","finding":"FMT from responders to PD-1 refractory melanoma patients can restore sensitivity to PD-1 inhibitors, with some patients achieving objective responses, though engraftment stability varies."}],"problem_or_question":"The review addresses the question of how the gut microbiome impacts the efficacy and toxicity of cancer immunotherapies, aiming to consolidate preclinical and clinical evidence to understand the rationale for microbiome-targeted therapies and identify gaps in current knowledge regarding predictive biomarkers and mechanistic pathways.","research_scope":"The review focuses on the role of the gut microbiome in modulating responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4 in patients with advanced solid tumors (melanoma, NSCLC, RCC, GI cancers). It covers preclinical evidence from mouse models, observational human data linking microbiota composition to clinical outcomes and adverse events, potential biological mechanisms, and early-phase clinical trials of microbiome-based interventions."}

identity.title: The role of the bacterial microbiome in the treatment of cancer

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为理解肠道微生物组如何调节实体瘤免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）疗效提供了重要的背景知识和机制框架。它详细列举了与ICI响应相关的特定细菌属（如Akkermansia, Bifidobacterium），并提出了代谢、免疫和易位三种主要机制。虽然它不直接回答所有具体分子通路问题，但为构建“微生物组-免疫-疗效”关联提供了关键的分类依据和现有证据汇总，特别适用于综述中关于“哪些菌群特征与治疗响应相关”以及“可能的生物学机制是什么”的部分。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述包含大量来自小鼠模型的研究结果，在将其应用于人类实体瘤时需注意物种差异和转化局限性。","不同研究中对“有利”或“不利”微生物群的界定存在不一致性，部分取决于癌症类型和测序方法，不能简单地将某一菌属在所有情况下都视为阳性或阴性标志物。","机制部分多为假设性或基于间接证据，具体分子通路尚未完全阐明，应避免将作者提出的机制当作已确证的结论。","综述未提供针对所有固体瘤类型的全面数据，重点在于黑色素瘤、NSCLC、RCC等，其他瘤种的数据较少或仅为初步发现。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了关于肠道和局部微生物组如何影响多种癌症治疗（特别是ICI和化疗）疗效及毒性的综合概览，并归纳了代谢、免疫和易位三大机制框架。","limits":"作为综述，其结论依赖于已发表研究的汇总，未进行新的实验验证。对于不同癌症类型中“有利微生物群”的差异性解释尚不充分，且许多机制仍处于假设阶段，需更多临床前和临床研究证实。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）治疗黑色素瘤、非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）、肾细胞癌（RCC）等","finding":"肠道微生物组显著影响ICI疗效。例如，Bacteroidetes在某些研究中与非响应者相关，而Bifidobacterium、Akkermansia muciniphila等与良好响应相关。抗生素预处理会因破坏微生物组多样性而降低ICI效率。"},{"conditions":"化疗（如环磷酰胺、奥沙利铂、伊立替康）","finding":"微生物组可通过调节宿主免疫（如促进Th17细胞产生）增强化疗疗效；也可通过代谢药物（如激活SN-38）导致严重腹泻等副作用。特定菌群（如Fusobacterium nucleatum）可能与化疗耐药有关。"},{"conditions":"放疗","finding":"微生物组主要影响放疗的副作用（如口腔黏膜炎、疲劳），而非直接决定疗效。调节微生物组（如使用益生菌）可减轻放疗损伤。"},{"conditions":"局部/肿瘤内微生物组（如胰腺癌、前列腺癌、肺癌）","finding":"肿瘤内微生物群可作为预后因子。例如，胰腺癌长期生存者的特定肿瘤微生物群可限制肿瘤生长；肺癌中肿瘤组织的微生物多样性低于正常组织，且特定菌属丰度变化与预后相关。"},{"conditions":"机制层面","finding":"微生物组通过代谢产物（如肌苷、短链脂肪酸）、激活抗原呈递细胞（APCs）、调节Treg/Th17平衡以及微生物易位至次级淋巴器官或肿瘤部位来影响治疗反应。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管已有研究报道特定细菌或病毒与癌症治疗疗效及毒性相关，但对宿主微生物组与癌症治疗反应之间相互作用的深入理解仍然有限。本文旨在全面回顾肠道和局部定居细菌微生物组在调节不同癌症治疗反应中的潜在作用，探讨其 probable mechanisms（可能机制），并为未来的研究方向提供计划和建议。","research_scope":"人类细菌微生物组（包括肠道、局部定居及肿瘤内微生物群）与癌症治疗反应之间的关系，涵盖免疫检查点抑制剂、化疗、放疗及其他疗法。"}

identity.title: Systematic evaluation of immune regulation and modulation

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt:
{"question_material":[{"examples":[{"attribution":"本研究","conditions":"适用于癌症免疫治疗临床试验中的微生物组监测；涉及不同解剖部位（主要是粪便，也包括皮肤、口腔、阴道）；对比了16S扩增子测序与宏基因组/宏转录组测序在分辨率、成本和生物信息学复杂性上的差异。","finding":"文章提出针对癌症免疫治疗研究中微生物组分析的标准化建议：
1. **标本采集与元数据**：强调标本采集和元数据显著影响下游分析。需确定感兴趣的解剖部位（如粪便、皮肤、口腔黏膜、阴道黏膜），因为空间分离较小的部位可能含有不同的细菌群落，因此采样一致性至关重要。大多数肿瘤研究聚焦于粪便，但其他部位也可提供独特信息。选择病例和对照、采样频率及方法时需考虑可行性（如自我收集）和患者参与度。
2. **测序策略选择**：
   - **16S rRNA基因测序**：最常用的方法，通过扩增和测序细菌16S rRNA基因的可变区域来确定微生物群的分类组成。由于新平台通常不测序完整基因，仅选择部分可变区域，这有助于有效鉴定属，但可能降低物种水平的识别能力。引物选择基于临床生物样本来源（如粪便样本常用V4引物，皮肤样本常用V1-3引物）以优化物种水平鉴定。Illumina MiSeq是最常用的平台。
   - **宏基因组测序（Shotgun Metagenomic Sequencing）**：分析样本中所有微生物的所有基因，不仅能鉴定细菌、真菌和病毒，还能识别群落中存在的基因和功能。最近还使用了宏转录组分析来评估哪些基因被转录及其程度。
3. **分析工具与比较**：
   - 16S数据分析常用QIIME和mothur等管道。
   - 宏基因组和宏转录组分析需要比扩增子测序更高的测序深度（导致更高成本），且生物信息学数据分析更具挑战性。","reference_ids":[],"use_in_review":"提供微生物样本采集、存储及测序分析（16S vs 宏基因组）的标准化建议流程，直接回答任务要求。"}],"explanation":"文章指出，微生物组在调节人体生理功能（特别是炎症和免疫）方面发挥重要作用，其组成变化可影响癌症的发生、进展及对治疗的反应。目前微生物组分析尚未成为癌症患者免疫评估的常规部分，但 emerging evidence 显示其具有重要潜力。

在标准化流程方面，核心原则是**标本采集的一致性和元数据的完整性**。由于不同身体部位的微生物群落具有特异性，且同一部位不同区域的微生物分布也可能存在差异，因此必须保持采样方法的一致性。对于粪便样本，考虑到可行性和患者依从性，自我收集是一种可行的策略。

在测序技术的选择上，文章阐述了两种主要路径的差异：
1. **16S rRNA基因测序**：这是一种基于扩增子的方法，通过靶向细菌16S rRNA基因的可变区域进行测序。其优势在于成本低、技术成熟，能有效鉴定到“属”的水平。然而，由于现代测序平台通常无法覆盖完整的16S基因，仅测序部分可变区，这限制了其在“种”水平上的分辨能力。引物的选择（如V4用于粪便，V1-3用于皮肤）对优化特定样本类型的物种鉴定至关重要。
2. **宏基因组测序**：这是一种无偏倚的方法，对样本中所有DNA进行测序。它不仅能提供微生物的分类学信息（包括细菌、真菌、病毒），还能提供功能基因信息（即微生物群落的代谢潜能）。此外，宏转录组测序可以揭示实际表达的基因。尽管宏基因组提供了更丰富的信息，但它需要更高的测序深度，从而带来更高的成本和更复杂的生物信息学分析挑战。

总体而言，标准化的关键在于根据研究目的（是需要快速、低成本的群落结构概览，还是需要高分辨率的物种鉴定或功能分析）选择合适的测序策略，并严格规范采样和元数据采集过程以确保结果的可重复性和临床相关性。","question_id":"Q01","remaining_points":["具体的粪便保存液类型或运输温度细节未在文中详细展开，仅提到需考虑可行性和患者参与。","未提及具体的DNA提取试剂盒或步骤的标准化建议。"]}]}

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文为综述“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤中免疫检查点抑制剂的疗效”提供了重要的背景信息和机制线索。它确认了微生物组在ICI疗效和irAEs（特别是结肠炎）中的作用，列举了关键菌属和干预手段（FMT），并强调了微生物组异质性的挑战。同时，它也提供了ICI在实体瘤中的疗效范围、毒性谱以及临床前模型局限性的广泛背景，有助于构建关于疗效调节机制和毒性管理的讨论框架。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["文中关于微生物组的发现主要来自黑色素瘤和部分实体瘤（NSCLC, 尿路上皮癌）的观察性研究，不能直接推广到所有实体瘤类型。","微生物组与疗效/毒性的关联多为相关性，因果机制（如分子模拟）仍需更多实验验证，避免将其视为既定事实。","临床前模型（如NHP）的局限性提示，任何基于动物模型的微生物组或免疫反应结论都需谨慎解读，可能存在物种特异性偏差。","作者强调微生物组异质性，因此在引用具体菌属时需注意其适用人群和癌种限制，避免过度概括。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了三类主要抗体疗法（ICI, BsAbs, ADCs）的irAEs系统性总结，包括具体药物、靶点、FDA警告及发生率数据。","limits":"作为综述，其数据来源于已发表的临床试验和FDA标签，未提供新的原始实验数据；对于特定罕见irAEs的因果机制仍多为假设或观察性关联。"},{"contribution":"指出了临床前安全性评估（特别是CRS检测）中标准化缺失的问题，并提出了参考抗体面板的概念。","limits":"所提出的标准化方案（如参考面板）仍处于早期验证阶段，尚未成为行业通用标准；不同实验室平台间的可比性仍需更多数据支持。"},{"contribution":"整合了微生物组、遗传标记（HLA, TMB）与ICI疗效及毒性之间的复杂关系。","limits":"许多关于微生物组和遗传标记的关联研究结果不一致或仅在特定癌种/队列中显著，难以直接外推至所有患者群体；因果关系尚未完全确立。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"ICI治疗（特别是CTLA-4抑制剂 vs PD-1/PD-L1抑制剂）","finding":"CTLA-4抑制剂通常比PD-1/PD-L1抑制剂引起更频繁和严重的irAEs（如高剂量伊匹木单抗的高级别毒性达38.6%-57.9%），而PD-1/PD-L1抑制剂的高级别不良事件发生率约为10%-15%。"},{"conditions":"BsAbs/BiTEs治疗（针对CD3等T细胞共刺激分子）","finding":"CD3靶向的双特异性抗体易引发强烈的多克隆T细胞激活，导致细胞因子释放综合征（CRS）和免疫效应细胞相关神经毒性综合征（ICANS）。疾病负荷高的患者CRS风险更高。"},{"conditions":"ADCs治疗（取决于连接子和载荷）","finding":"ADCs的毒性不仅取决于靶点，还强烈依赖于连接子的稳定性和载荷的性质。例如，MMAE载荷易导致神经病变，而某些载荷或过早释放可能导致肝毒性（如VOD）或眼毒性。"},{"conditions":"宿主微生物组与ICI疗效/毒性关联","finding":"肠道微生物组组成影响ICI疗效和irAEs（如结肠炎）。特定菌属（如Ruminococcaceae, Akkermansia）与响应者相关。粪菌移植（FMT）在难治性黑色素瘤中显示出改善疗效的潜力，但微生物组异质性增加了复杂性。"},{"conditions":"临床前模型评估CRS风险","finding":"传统的非人灵长类动物模型未能完全重现人类的淋巴细胞活化毒性（如TGN1412试验失败案例）。体外全血或PBMC测定法受相态（固体vs水相）和细胞比例影响大，实验室间变异性高，亟需标准化参考物质和协议。"}],"problem_or_question":"抗体类癌症免疫疗法虽然有效，但受到严重且可能危及生命的免疫相关不良事件（irAEs）的限制。现有的理解尚不足以完全预测个体患者的毒性反应，且临床前模型在模拟人类免疫反应方面存在局限。本研究旨在梳理现有知识，识别毒性机制，评估当前风险评估工具的不足，并为未来更安全的药物设计和临床前筛选提供方向。","research_scope":"抗体类生物药物（包括免疫检查点抑制剂ICI、双特异性抗体BsAbs/BiTEs、抗体偶联药物ADCs）在癌症治疗中引发的免疫相关不良事件（irAEs），特别是细胞因子释放综合征（CRS）及其他器官毒性。"}

It also outlines the cellular mechanisms (T-cell infiltration, antigen presentation, cGAS-interferon-β pathway) and discusses intervention strategies like FMT and probiotics, noting their variable efficacy and context-dependency. This material is essential for explaining the 'how' and 'what mechanisms' aspects of the review question.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review emphasizes that microbial effects are highly context-dependent and vary by host genetics, diet, antibiotic exposure, and tumor type. Preclinical models (mice) differ significantly from human microbiomes.","Intervention strategies like probiotics and FMT have shown inconsistent clinical outcomes. Probiotic use may even be detrimental in some contexts. Caution is needed when interpreting these as universally beneficial solutions.","The review synthesizes diverse mechanisms (enzymatic, metabolic, signaling, immune, senescence) into an integrated network, but this is a conceptual framework. Individual mechanisms should be evaluated based on the strength of evidence provided for each specific pathway."]}

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文为综述提供了关于“癌症类型特异性微生物标志物”的关键实证素材。它挑战了跨癌种通用的微生物预测模型（如A. muciniphila作为通用增效菌的假设），并提出了“既往内分泌治疗史”可能重塑微生物组对ICI反应的影响这一重要视角。同时，其纵向数据证明了ICI治疗本身对微生物组的稳定性，排除了药物急性干扰作为主要混淆因素的可能性。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该研究结果严格限定于“恩杂鲁胺治疗进展后”的mCRPC患者，其微生物组状态深受既往内分泌治疗影响，不能直接推广至未经内分泌治疗的前列腺癌患者或初治实体瘤患者。","A. muciniphila在反应者中的减少与多数其他ICI研究相反，这可能与前列腺癌的特定病理生理环境（如肌苷促转移风险）或既往用药有关，解读时需避免将其视为普适规律。","S. salivarius的发现虽显著，但其具体免疫调节机制在本研究中仅为推测，需结合其他功能学研究谨慎引用。","样本量较小（n=23），发现的差异丰度菌群可能存在假阳性风险，尤其是qPCR验证仅针对少数几个菌种。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了首个针对mCRPC患者在接受ICI治疗前/初期微生物组特征的系统描述，揭示了该人群中特有的微生物-反应关联模式（如S. salivarius的正向关联和A. muciniphila的负向关联）。","limits":"样本量较小（n=23），统计效力有限；仅使用16S rRNA测序而非宏基因组，分辨率受限；未深入探讨具体的代谢机制或因果路径；结果可能受既往恩杂鲁胺治疗、饮食、地理因素等混杂因素影响；作者承认部分分类学鉴定存在不确定性（如Roseburia属）。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"First Timepoint cohort (n=23), 16S sequencing & qPCR","finding":"整体α和β多样性在反应者与非反应者间无显著差异；个体间变异占主导（~50%）。"},{"conditions":"First Timepoint cohort, GLM analysis of multiple hypervariable regions","finding":"Streptococcus salivarius在反应者粪便中显著富集（p=0.004），且qPCR证实该趋势；但该菌在口腔漱口水中的水平与反应无关，且口腔与粪便水平不相关。"},{"conditions":"First Timepoint cohort, 16S sequencing (V6-7 region) & qPCR","finding":"Akkermansia muciniphila在反应者中显著降低（与黑色素瘤等其他癌症报道相反），qPCR确认了这一减少趋势。"},{"conditions":"Longitudinal analysis (n=9 patients across treatment cycles)","finding":"帕博利珠单抗治疗未引起全局微生物组成的显著变化；个体内样本聚类紧密，时间点对变异贡献极小（<3%）。"},{"conditions":"Application of Shaikh et al. integrated index","finding":"该综合指数未能区分本队列中的反应者与非反应者，表明不同癌症类型或治疗史可能导致微生物信号的特异性。"}],"problem_or_question":"既往研究表明肠道微生物影响ICI疗效，但在mCRPC背景下，特别是经过雄激素受体抑制剂（如恩杂鲁胺）预处理后的患者中，微生物组特征如何预测帕博利珠单抗的治疗反应？是否存在不同于其他实体瘤（如黑色素瘤）的微生物标志物？","research_scope":"转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）患者，在恩杂鲁胺治疗进展后接受抗PD-1免疫检查点抑制剂（帕博利珠单抗）治疗。样本为粪便和口腔漱口水DNA。"}

identity.title: The role of the gut microbiome on the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in Japanese responder patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer.

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该研究提供了关于肠道微生物组如何关联固体肿瘤（NSCLC）免疫治疗疗效的直接观察数据。其核心价值在于指出了特定细菌属（有益菌与有害菌）与临床预后（TTF）的方向性关联，尽管由于样本量限制，部分关联未达到统计学显著性。对于综述而言，它提供了具体的“菌-效应”对应关系素材，特别是关于Bilophila与较差预后的负向关联，以及Lactobacillus/Clostridium的正向趋势，可用于支持或反驳不同研究中微生物组对ICI疗效影响的异质性。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该研究样本量极小（17例），统计效力不足，许多具有生物学意义的趋势（如Lactobacillus）未达到统计学显著性。解读时应避免夸大其确定性，应视为探索性证据。","研究对象仅限于日本NSCLC患者，且均为长期治疗者（>3个月），存在严重的选择偏倚（幸存者偏差）。结果可能不适用于早期治疗失败者或其他种族群体。","作者提出的机制（如Lactobacillus促进DC成熟）是基于文献综述的推测，本研究并未提供直接的分子或细胞水平证据。在综述中引用时，必须明确区分这是作者的假设还是本研究的实证结果。","Bilophila高丰度与延长TTF（更好疗效）的关联可能与部分其他研究报道的负面作用相反，这突显了微生物组研究的高度情境依赖性和潜在矛盾，需谨慎对待单一研究的结论。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"在亚洲（日本）NSCLC人群中，初步识别出与ICI疗效相关的特定肠道细菌属（如Lactobacillus, Clostridium, Bilophila等），提供了微生物组作为潜在疗效生物标志物的观察性证据。","limits":"样本量极小（仅17例），存在选择偏倚（仅纳入治疗>3个月的患者，可能排除早期进展或不耐受者）；单中心回顾性研究；仅采集单次粪便样本，无法反映治疗前后菌群动态变化；未控制抗生素使用等混杂因素的具体细节（虽记录但未深入校正）；部分关键图表不可读，具体统计细节受限。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"对比ICI反应者（n=6）与非反应者（n=11）的肠道菌群组成","finding":"反应者的肠道菌群中乳酸杆菌（Lactobacillus）、梭菌属（Clostridium）和Syntrophococcus显著富集；非反应者中Bilophila、Sutterella和Parabacteroides显著富集。"},{"conditions":"特定细菌属丰度与治疗失败时间（TTF）的关系","finding":"高丰度的Bilophila与显著延长的TTF相关（HR 6.27, P=0.0037）。高丰度的Lactobacillus和Clostridium倾向于延长TTF，但统计学上不显著（P分别为0.219和0.352）。Syntrophococcus高丰度也显示延长TTF的趋势（P=0.057）。Parabacteroides丰度与TTF无显著关联。"},{"conditions":"肠道菌群Alpha多样性","finding":"反应者与非反应者之间的Alpha多样性无显著差异，且未影响TTF。"}],"problem_or_question":"在晚期NSCLC患者中，是否存在特定的肠道微生物组特征可以作为预测免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）长期疗效的生物标志物？目前缺乏能够筛选出能从ICI中长期获益患者的强效生物标志物。","research_scope":"日本晚期非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）患者，接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗超过3个月的人群。样本量为17例，分为反应者（R, n=6）和非反应者（NR, n=11）。"}

identity.title: The Gut Microbiome and Cancer Immunotherapy: Can We Use the Gut Microbiome as a Predictive Biomarker for Clinical Response in Cancer Immunotherapy?

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文提供了关于肠道微生物组如何影响实体瘤免疫治疗疗效的临床证据汇总，特别指出了特定菌群（如Faecalibacterium, Akkermansia）与疗效的正向关联，以及抗生素使用或特定菌群缺失与疗效不佳或毒性的关联。此外，它提供了FMT作为克服免疫耐药的临床干预案例，是讨论微生物组调控机制和临床转化潜力的重要素材。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述仅纳入临床研究，排除了动物实验，因此其关于机制的解释（如T细胞激活）主要基于人类临床样本的相关性或FMT后的表型变化，而非直接的分子通路解析。","发现的菌群与疗效的关联多为观察性结果，存在混杂因素（如饮食、生活方式、合并用药），不能直接视为因果证据，除非有FMT等干预性研究的支持。","不同研究间使用的测序区域（V3-V4, V4, V4-V5）和分析方法不同，导致具体菌种鉴定可能存在偏差，比较时需考虑技术异质性。","FMT研究样本量极小（n=10, n=15），结果仅代表初步安全性和可行性，不能代表普遍疗效。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"首次专门针对临床研究的综述，汇总了肠道微生物组作为ICIs疗效预测生物标志物和irAEs风险因子的证据，强调了FMT在逆转耐药性方面的初步临床可行性。","limits":"所纳入的研究样本量普遍较小（多数n≤42），存在异质性（不同癌症类型、不同ICI药物、不同测序方法如16S rRNA与宏基因组）。观察性研究无法确立因果关系。未对纳入的非随机研究进行严格的质量偏倚风险评估。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"接受ICIs治疗的晚期癌症患者（黑色素瘤、HCC、NSCLC等）","finding":"基线肠道微生物组的多样性和组成与ICIs疗效显著相关。高α-多样性通常与较长的PFS和OS相关。特定菌属富集与响应正相关（如Fecalibacterium prausnitzii, Bifidobacterium longum, Akkermansia muciniphila），而某些拟杆菌目（Bacteroidales）丰度高则与非响应相关。"},{"conditions":"接受CTLA-4抑制剂治疗的黑色素瘤患者","finding":"低丰度的Bacteroidetes门细菌与免疫检查点抑制剂诱导的结肠炎（GI毒性）相关；相反，较高的Bacteroidetes丰度与抵抗结肠炎发生相关。"},{"conditions":"抗PD-1难治性转移性黑色素瘤患者接受来自响应者的FMT","finding":"两项突破性临床试验显示，将来自免疫治疗响应者的粪菌移植给难治性患者，结合抗PD-1治疗，可使部分患者重新获得临床响应（Baruch et al. 3/10响应；Davar et al. 6/15响应），且安全性良好。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管免疫疗法提高了部分晚期癌症患者的生存率，但仅少数患者受益且常伴随严重免疫相关不良事件（irAEs）。目前尚缺乏基于临床证据的指导方针来利用肠道微生物组预测治疗反应或管理副作用。本研究试图厘清肠道微生物组作为预测生物标志物的潜力及其在增强疗效和减少副作用中的作用。","research_scope":"临床癌症患者（晚期转移性黑色素瘤、肝细胞癌、非小细胞肺癌及肾细胞癌），聚焦于免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）治疗前后的肠道微生物组特征及其与疗效和不良事件的关系。"}
