identity.title: Microbiome and cancer: mechanistic insights, diagnostic potential, and therapeutic strategies

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为理解肠道微生物组如何调节实体瘤免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）疗效提供了详尽的机制背景和多层次证据。它不仅列出了与良好/不良预后相关的特定菌种，还深入解析了四种核心机制（抗原呈递、T细胞启动、代谢物调节、抗原模拟），并讨论了 FMT 等干预措施的临床前和早期临床结果。这对于回答“微生物组如何调节 ICIs 疗效”及其“介导机制”两个子问题具有极高的参考价值，可直接用于构建关于微生物-免疫互作在治疗响应中作用的章节。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述强调微生物组效应的‘情境依赖性’（context-dependent），例如 SCFAs 在不同肿瘤背景下可能具有相反的作用，避免将其概括为单一的‘好’或‘坏’。","区分因果证据（如 H. pylori 与胃癌）和相关性证据（许多测序发现的菌种），在引用时需注意证据等级。","FMT 在癌症治疗中的应用目前主要处于早期临床试验阶段，其长期安全性和有效性尚未确立，不应过度推断其临床普及度。","不同研究使用的微生物分析方法（16S vs 宏基因组）和数据分析流程存在差异，可能导致结果不一致，比较时需考虑方法学异质性。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了微生物组影响癌症免疫治疗（特别是 ICIs）机制的综合框架，包括抗原呈递、T细胞启动、代谢物调节和抗原模拟四个主要途径。","limits":"作为综述，其结论依赖于引用的原始研究，本身不提供新的实验数据；许多机制主要在动物模型中验证，临床相关性仍需更大规模试验确认。"},{"contribution":"总结了微生物组介导的药物代谢对化疗毒性和疗效的影响，为个性化用药提供理论依据。","limits":"具体微生物酶对药物代谢的贡献在不同患者间存在高度变异性，标准化检测方法尚缺乏。"},{"contribution":"评估了基于微生物组的诊断生物标志物的潜力，涵盖了多种样本类型和分析方法。","limits":"多数诊断标志物仍处于验证阶段，缺乏大规模前瞻性临床试验的支持，且受个体差异和方法学标准化不足的限制。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"针对免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）治疗的患者队列及小鼠模型","finding":"特定的肠道微生物组成（如 Akkermansia muciniphila, Bifidobacterium spp.）与改善的 ICIs 疗效相关，而抗生素使用导致的菌群失调则降低疗效。粪菌移植（FMT）从响应者转移到非响应者可恢复抗肿瘤免疫反应。"},{"conditions":"结直肠癌（CRC）和其他实体瘤的微环境","finding":"肿瘤相关微生物（如 Fusobacterium nucleatum）通过直接定植肿瘤组织，抑制 NK 细胞和 T 细胞毒性，促进免疫逃逸和化疗耐药。"},{"conditions":"微生物代谢物对宿主细胞的影响","finding":"短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）具有双重作用：在正常结肠上皮中维持稳态，但在肿瘤微环境中可能通过促进调节性 T 细胞（Tregs）扩张而抑制抗肿瘤免疫；次级胆汁酸和 LPS 促进炎症和肿瘤进展。"},{"conditions":"微生物毒素的作用机制","finding":"特定微生物毒素（如 colibactin, BFT, CagA）通过诱导 DNA 双链断裂、破坏上皮屏障或激活致癌信号通路，直接驱动基因组不稳定性及肿瘤发生。"},{"conditions":"微生物组作为诊断工具","finding":"粪便、唾液和血液中的微生物特征（如 F. nucleatum 增加，F. prausnitzii 减少）可作为多种癌症（特别是 CRC 和胰腺癌）的非侵入性早期检测和预后生物标志物，结合机器学习可提高准确性。"}],"problem_or_question":"旨在全面理解微生物组在癌症生物学中的复杂作用，整合机制性、临床前和临床证据，以阐明微生物组如何驱动肿瘤发生、重塑肿瘤微环境、影响治疗反应，并评估其作为诊断工具和 therapeutic target 的转化潜力。","research_scope":"人类微生物组（包括细菌、病毒、真菌及其代谢物）与癌症生物学之间的相互作用，涵盖肿瘤发生机制、治疗反应调节、诊断生物标志物开发及基于微生物组的干预策略。重点涉及胃肠道癌症（如结直肠癌、胃癌）、黑色素瘤及其他实体瘤中的微生物-宿主互作。"}

identity.title: Tarloxotinib targets tumor hypoxia to improve therapeutic efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition in a TLR9 dependent manner

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"本文提供了关于“缺氧靶向药物如何通过重塑肿瘤微环境和激活先天免疫信号来克服免疫检查点抑制剂耐药”的具体实证素材。它特别适用于解释非微生物因素（如缺氧和TLR9信号）如何影响ICI疗效，以及HAP类药物作为ICI增敏剂的机制。虽然不直接涉及肠道菌群，但其关于TME重塑、细胞因子风暴和免疫细胞浸润的数据可作为对比或背景，用于讨论不同干预手段（如菌群调节 vs 缺氧调节）在改善ICI疗效上的异同。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["本文是临床前小鼠研究，其发现的机制（如TLR9依赖性）和疗效数据不能直接外推至人类患者的临床结果，尽管作者引用了早期临床试验的安全性数据。","TLR9激活是tarloxotinib的一个独特属性，并非所有HAP或ICI增敏剂都具备此机制，解读时需注意其特异性。","研究中使用的肿瘤模型（MB49, MC38, EG7.OVA）均为同系瘤，可能无法完全代表人类实体瘤的异质性和复杂性。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"揭示了tarloxotinib作为HAP的双重机制：既通过消除缺氧改善TME物理屏障，又通过TLR9激活产生免疫刺激信号，从而协同增强ICI疗效。","limits":"所给摘要未交代具体的剂量优化过程及长期耐药机制；所有数据均基于小鼠模型，尚未提供人体临床试验的直接疗效证据（仅引用既往Phase I/II的安全性数据）。"},{"contribution":"证实了TLR9信号通路在HAP类药物增强ICI疗效中的关键中介作用，为小分子TLR9激动剂的系统性给药提供了新策略。","limits":"TLR9激活的具体配体身份未在文中明确鉴定；不同肿瘤类型（EGFR依赖vs非依赖）对TLR9信号的敏感性差异机制尚需进一步探索。"},{"contribution":"提供了tarloxotinib与ICI联用不增加间质性肺病风险的临床前证据，解决了EGFR-TKI与ICI联用的主要安全顾虑。","limits":"肺部安全性仅在短期实验中评估，长期累积毒性未知；其他潜在器官毒性（如皮肤、肠道）的详细量化数据有限。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"MB49同系肿瘤模型，tarloxotinib单药 vs 对照","finding":"tarloxotinib将肿瘤缺氧分数从9.56%显著降低至1.19%（约8倍降幅），并抑制EGFR下游信号传导。"},{"conditions":"MB49模型，tarloxotinib + 抗PD-L1联合治疗","finding":"相比单药，联合治疗显著提高完全缓解率（达到100%），肿瘤生长延迟增加>360%，生存期显著延长。肿瘤内CD8+ T细胞浸润比例从8%增至43%。"},{"conditions":"MyD88 KO或TLR9 KO小鼠，tarloxotinib + 抗PD-L1","finding":"在野生型小鼠中观察到的联合治疗协同效应被完全阻断，血清促炎细胞因子（IL-6, IL-12p40, IFNγ等）产生减少，表明该效应依赖于TLR9/MyD88信号通路。"},{"conditions":"EGFR非依赖性模型（MC38, EG7.OVA），tarloxotinib + ICI","finding":"尽管tarloxotinib单药对这些模型无效（因缺乏EGFR靶点），但与ICI联合仍能显著延缓肿瘤生长，证明其免疫调节作用独立于EGFR抑制。"},{"conditions":"安全性评估，tarloxotinib + 抗PD-L1","finding":"联合治疗未引起小鼠体重显著下降，且肺部组织病理学显示无胶原沉积增加，排除了间质性肺病（ILD）的发生。"}],"problem_or_question":"1. 肿瘤缺氧如何导致ICI耐药？2. 能否利用tarloxotinib这一缺氧激活药物来逆转缺氧并改善ICI疗效？3. tarloxotinib与ICI联用的具体免疫学机制是什么，是否依赖于特定的信号通路（如TLR9）？4. 这种联合疗法是否具有安全性，特别是是否会引发EGFR-TKI与ICI联用常见的间质性肺病（ILD）？","research_scope":"本研究使用小鼠同系肿瘤模型（MB49膀胱癌、MC38结直肠癌、EG7.OVA淋巴瘤）及体外细胞实验，评估临床阶段缺氧激活前药tarloxotinib与免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI，特别是抗PD-L1）联合治疗的抗肿瘤疗效及其机制。研究对象为实体瘤微环境中的缺氧状态、免疫细胞浸润及TLR9信号通路。"}

identity.title: Impact of influenza vaccination on survival of patients with advanced cancer receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (INVIDIa-2): final results of the multicentre, prospective, observational study

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文提供了关于非微生物类外部免疫刺激（流感疫苗）如何影响ICI疗效的观察性证据。虽然不直接涉及肠道菌群，但其提出的“旁观者效应”（bystander effect）和免疫超激活机制，可作为解释其他免疫调节因素（包括可能的微生物抗原交叉反应或系统性炎症）增强ICI疗效的理论参照。同时，其关于肿瘤类型异质性的发现（肺癌获益明显，黑色素瘤不明显）可为综述中讨论不同瘤种对免疫微环境干预的反应差异提供对比案例。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该研究为观察性设计，发现的关联不等于因果；作者声称的“协同作用”是基于统计学关联和理论推测，需结合其他实验研究验证。","结果高度依赖于倾向评分匹配的准确性，且未测量混杂因素（如社会经济地位、生活方式细节、具体合并用药）可能仍影响结果。","不同肿瘤类型的异质性结果提示，不能将流感疫苗对肺癌的获益外推至所有实体瘤，尤其是黑色素瘤在此研究中未显示OS获益。","材料中未提供具体的免疫学机制数据（如细胞因子水平、T细胞功能检测），因此关于“旁观者效应”的解释属于作者的理论框架，而非本研究的直接实证发现。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了首个大规模前瞻性观察性证据，表明在晚期实体瘤患者接受ICI治疗期间接种流感疫苗不仅安全，且可能与更好的OS、PFS和DCR相关，排除了疫苗对ICI疗效的负面干扰假设。","limits":"研究为观察性设计，存在选择偏倚（尽管通过PSM校正，但无法完全消除未测量混杂因素）；缺乏生物标志物相关性分析以验证免疫机制；受COVID-19大流行影响，治疗连续性和随访可能存在异质性；不同肿瘤类型的获益程度不一致（如黑色素瘤无显著OS获益）。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"倾向评分匹配后的队列（N=1004），中位随访20个月","finding":"接种疫苗组的总生存期（OS）显著长于未接种组（27.0个月 vs 20.9个月，HR 0.75, p=0.005）"},{"conditions":"倾向评分匹配后的队列","finding":"接种疫苗组的无进展生存期（PFS）显著长于未接种组（12.5个月 vs 9.6个月，p=0.049）"},{"conditions":"倾向评分匹配后的队列","finding":"接种疫苗组的疾病控制率（DCR）显著高于未接种组（74.7% vs 66.5%，OR 1.47, p=0.007）"},{"conditions":"按原发肿瘤亚组分析","finding":"OS的获益在肺癌和肾癌亚组中临床意义明显，但在黑色素瘤、头颈癌和其他类型中未见显著差异；PFS、DCR和ORR在不同肿瘤类型间表现相对一致"}],"problem_or_question":"在晚期癌症患者接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗期间，接种流感疫苗是否会对免疫治疗的疗效产生不利影响（如干扰T细胞反应或降低抗肿瘤活性），或者是否存在潜在的协同获益？此前缺乏针对这一特定人群的大规模前瞻性数据。","research_scope":"意大利82家肿瘤中心收治的接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗的晚期实体瘤患者；观察性队列研究，重点分析流感疫苗接种状态对免疫治疗结局的影响。"}

identity.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated gastrointestinal adverse events in patients with colorectal cancer

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文提供了结直肠癌（特别是MSI-H亚型）患者使用ICI时的胃肠道毒性基线数据，并构建了“肿瘤微环境-肠道微生物组-免疫疗效/毒性”的理论框架。对于综述而言，其核心价值在于提供特定癌种下的毒性发生率参考，以及阐述微生物组如何通过重塑肿瘤免疫微环境间接影响ICI疗效和irAEs风险的机制假说。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该研究为回顾性分析，样本量有限，结果可能存在选择偏倚，不宜作为普适性结论。","关于肠道微生物组的论述主要基于文献回顾和假设，本研究本身未提供直接的微生物组测序数据或干预实验结果。","IMC的低严重程度可能与MSI-H特定的肿瘤微环境有关，但这仅是作者的推测，尚未在本研究中得到机制层面的证实。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了MSI-H结直肠癌患者中ICI相关结肠炎的具体发病率（3.8%）和临床分级分布数据；初步提出肿瘤微环境可能解释IMC低严重性的假设。","limits":"所给摘要未交代具体的统计模型细节、多变量校正因素及对照组设置；样本量较小（仅18例IMC患者），且为单中心回顾性研究，存在选择偏倚风险；未能直接量化肠道微生物组的影响，仅将其列为未来研究方向。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"474名接受ICI治疗的CRC患者，随访至末次给药后3个月","finding":"18例（3.8%）发生IMC；主要人群为白人（88.8%）、男性（61.1%），中位年龄69.5岁"},{"conditions":"IMC患者亚组分析","finding":"50%接受抗PD-1/L1联合CTLA-4治疗；66.6%为MSI-H CRC；61.2%为1-2级结肠炎，66.7%为1-2级腹泻"},{"conditions":"内镜评估与治疗反应","finding":"5例接受内镜评估，2例显示溃疡性炎症需生物制剂免疫抑制治疗；61.1%因毒性暂停治疗；大多数接受类固醇治疗"},{"conditions":"其他器官毒性对比","finding":"41.4%出现2级肝毒性，5.8%出现2级胰腺毒性，提示IMC严重程度可能低于其他ICI相关毒性"}],"problem_or_question":"明确MSI-H结直肠癌患者在接受ICI治疗时，ICI相关结肠炎（IMC）的发病率和具体临床特征；探讨肿瘤微环境及潜在的肠道微生物组对IMC严重程度的影响机制。","research_scope":"2014年6月1日至2022年12月31日期间接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗的成人结直肠癌（CRC）患者，重点观察微卫星不稳定性高（MSI-H）亚型及ICI相关结肠炎（IMC）的发生特征。"}

identity.title: Microbiome-selective DNA Pol IIIC inhibitors in oncology infection management

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该文献为综述提供了关于“抗生素类型对微生物组影响进而调节ICI疗效”这一路径的关键对比素材。它引入了DNA Pol IIIC抑制剂作为区别于传统广谱抗生素的新兴类别，强调了其“微生物组 sparing”特性，可用于解释为何某些抗生素暴露对ICI疗效负面影响较小，或作为未来干预策略的理论依据。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["本文是观点性文章，其提出的“DNA Pol IIIC抑制剂类具有广泛的微生物组保护效应”主要基于会议报告和初步数据，需谨慎对待其普适性。","文中提到的微生物组保护效果是在C. difficile感染治疗背景下观察到的，不能直接外推至所有类型的细菌感染或所有肿瘤类型。","作者声称的“直接肿瘤学治疗目标”是基于理论推导，尚未在本研究中通过随机对照试验证实。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提出了将微生物组保护作为肿瘤感染管理直接治疗目标的观点，连接了抗感染治疗与ICI疗效。","limits":"本文为观点性文章，非原始实证研究；缺乏针对实体瘤患者使用此类抗生素后ICI疗效的具体临床结局数据；部分结论基于会议报告，尚未经过完整同行评审发表。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"肿瘤患者（化疗或造血干细胞移植后）","finding":"高达60%的患者发生感染并发症，20-30%需要住院；广谱抗生素暴露与ICI治疗后总生存期减少30-50%，无进展生存期减少25-40%。"},{"conditions":"使用DNA Pol IIIC抑制剂（如ibezapolstat）治疗艰难梭菌感染","finding":"临床治愈率达88-96%，复发率显著低于标准疗法；定量宏基因组分析显示保留了Bacteroidetes和Firmicutes门，维持了alpha多样性，并减少了肠杆菌目的扩张。"},{"conditions":"IDWeek 2025会议数据","finding":"微生物组保护效应可能是Pol IIIC抑制剂类的广泛特性，有粪便药物浓度研究和纵向耐药组图谱支持。"}],"problem_or_question":"解决肿瘤患者因使用广谱抗生素导致的肠道微生物组失调问题，该问题与免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）疗效降低及感染复发密切相关。","research_scope":"肿瘤学感染管理，特别是接受化疗或造血干细胞移植的患者中细菌感染的抗生素选择及其对肠道微生物组和免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）疗效的影响。"}

identity.title: Insights into the Relationship Between the Gut Microbiome and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Solid Tumors

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review serves as a high-level map of the field, identifying consistent microbial signals (taxa and metabolites) across different solid tumors and summarizing the evidence for microbiota-based interventions. It is particularly useful for establishing the landscape of known biomarkers and the rationale for modulation strategies, while highlighting the heterogeneity that prevents a single universal signature.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The paper is a narrative review; its findings represent a synthesis of existing literature, not new primary data.","Specific bacterial associations may vary significantly based on patient geography, diet, and baseline health status, limiting generalizability.","Mechanistic claims are often based on preclinical models; human applicability should be treated as hypothesis-generating unless supported by robust clinical trial data cited within the review.","The term 'solid tumors' is broad; associations found in melanoma may not apply to GI cancers due to distinct microbial environments."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Provides a comprehensive synthesis of microbiome signatures associated with ICI response across major solid tumor types. Identifies key candidate biomarkers (e.g., Akkermansia, Faecalibacterium) and mechanistic links (metabolites, T-cell activation). Catalogs ongoing clinical trials, offering a roadmap for future research directions.","limits":"As a narrative review, it aggregates heterogeneous data from various studies with differing methodologies, sample sizes, and sequencing techniques. It does not provide primary experimental validation or a standardized meta-analysis. The 'universal' microbiome signature remains elusive due to confounding factors like geography, diet, and genetics, which the authors acknowledge but cannot resolve within this format."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"Melanoma & Cutaneous SCC","finding":"Responders show enrichment of Faecalibacterium, Ruminococcaceae, Bifidobacterium, and Akkermansia; non-responders have higher Bacteroides and Escherichia coli. Specific metabolites like desaminotyrosine (from Clostridium orbiscindens) and indole-3-carboxaldehyde modulate immune responses."},{"conditions":"Thoracic Cancers (NSCLC/SCLC) & RCC","finding":"Akkermansia muciniphila is linked to improved survival in NSCLC and RCC. Butyrate-producing bacteria (Faecalibacterium, Roseburia) are enriched in responders. Antibiotic use prior to ICI correlates with reduced efficacy. High alpha diversity generally associates with better outcomes."},{"conditions":"Gastrointestinal Malignancies","finding":"Helicobacter pylori infection correlates with poorer outcomes in gastric cancer. Fusobacterium abundance in tumor microbiome relates to shorter survival in esophageal cancer. Coprobacillus cateniformis reduces PD-L2 expression, potentially enhancing immunity."},{"conditions":"Microbiota Modulation Interventions","finding":"FMT from ICI responders to non-responders (or mice) can restore sensitivity to ICIs. Probiotics (e.g., Enterococcus, Bifidobacterium) and dietary fiber intake are associated with improved PFS/OS trends. Vitamin B5 supplementation enhances PD-L1 blockade efficacy in models."}],"problem_or_question":"To understand the complex relationship between the gut microbiome and ICI efficacy/safety in solid tumors, identify potential microbial biomarkers for predicting response, and explore how microbiota modulation can improve clinical outcomes.","research_scope":"Solid tumors (specifically melanoma, cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, thoracic malignancies, renal cell carcinoma, and gastrointestinal malignancies); the relationship between gut microbiome composition/metabolites and the efficacy/toxicity of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs)."}

identity.title: The Impact of Gut Microbiota-Derived Metabolites on the Tumor Immune Microenvironment

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为回答“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤中免疫检查点抑制剂的疗效”及其“介导机制”提供了丰富的理论背景和具体分子证据。它特别擅长梳理微生物代谢物（而非仅仅是细菌种类）如何通过代谢重编程、表观遗传修饰和受体信号传导直接影响T细胞和巨噬细胞的功能，从而解释ICI疗效差异的潜在生物学基础。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述主要关注代谢物层面的机制，对于细菌菌株特异性（非代谢物依赖）的机制涉及较少，需注意区分。","文中提到的许多机制来自小鼠模型（如C57BL/6），其在人体中的适用性可能存在差异，特别是在药物代谢和免疫反应方面。","对于“肿瘤内微生物”的来源和功能，文章指出目前仍存在争议（是主动定植还是被动滞留），需谨慎解读其因果作用。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"系统性地分类和总结了多种肠道微生物代谢物（SCFAs、胆汁酸、肌苷、色氨酸衍生物等）对实体瘤免疫微环境中不同免疫细胞（T细胞、巨噬细胞等）的具体调节机制，提供了从分子水平理解微生物-免疫互作的框架。","limits":"作为综述，其结论依赖于所引用的原始研究，本身不提供新的实验数据。对于某些代谢物的作用存在情境依赖性（如在PDAC中色氨酸衍生物促癌，而在其他背景下可能有益），文章指出了这种复杂性但未给出统一的预测规则。此外，关于代谢物在人体内的实际递送效率和长期安全性数据尚不充分，主要基于动物模型和体外实验。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"在黑色素瘤和胰腺癌的小鼠模型中","finding":"丁酸盐（butyrate）和戊酸盐（valerate）通过增强mTOR复合物活性和诱导颗粒酶B表达，提高了细胞毒性T淋巴细胞（CTLs）的杀伤能力；体外实验中，SCFAs处理增强了CAR-T细胞分泌TNFα和IFN-γ的能力。"},{"conditions":"在多种实体瘤模型中联合抗CTLA-4治疗","finding":"肌苷（inosine）通过调节T细胞上的腺苷A2A受体，显著增强了免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）的疗效，增加了产生IFN-γ的Th1细胞频率。"},{"conditions":"在三阴性乳腺癌（TNBC）中","finding":"微生物代谢物氧化三甲胺（TMAO）在具有活跃免疫微环境的肿瘤中丰富，并促进了抗肿瘤免疫反应。"},{"conditions":"在胰腺导管腺癌（PDAC）中","finding":"肠道乳酸杆菌将饮食色氨酸转化为吲哚类衍生物，激活肿瘤相关巨噬细胞（TAMs）中的芳香烃受体（AhR），从而促进TAMs的促肿瘤功能；去除饮食色氨酸可减少AhR活性并增加CD8+ T细胞浸润。"},{"conditions":"在结直肠癌（CRC）中","finding":"甲酸盐（formate）和异戊酸盐（isovalerate）被鉴定为致癌代谢物，促进癌细胞侵袭和转移；次级胆汁酸可诱导DNA损伤并调节免疫微环境。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管已知肠道微生物群影响癌症发展和免疫治疗反应，但具体的分子机制，特别是微生物代谢物如何直接塑造TME中的免疫细胞功能，尚不完全清楚。本文试图系统总结现有证据，阐明这些代谢物在调节抗肿瘤免疫中的具体作用，并评估其作为治疗靶点的潜力。","research_scope":"综述聚焦于肠道微生物群及其衍生的代谢物与实体瘤免疫微环境（TME）之间的相互作用，涵盖细菌、真菌等微生物群落对肿瘤发生、进展及免疫治疗反应的影响。"}

identity.title: Metagenomics and culturomics reveal the dual role of the gut microbiome in the development of immune-related toxicities and the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in cancer

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This paper offers concrete mechanistic insights into how the gut microbiome modulates ICI efficacy, specifically addressing the 'dual role' of certain bacteria in causing toxicity while boosting anti-tumor immunity. It provides a rare example of a single bacterial species (Paraclostridium bifermentans) being functionally linked to both irAE and efficacy, distinguishing between live-bacteria-dependent inflammatory effects and metabolite-mediated immunostimulatory effects. This is valuable for explaining mechanisms where microbial components directly influence host physiology and immune response.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The study identifies P. bifermentans as a key player, but the exact metabolite responsible for the anti-tumor effect is not characterized; do not overstate the specificity of the molecular mechanism.","Mouse models used (MCA-205, DSS) have limitations in fully recapitulating human ir-colitis; results should be framed as preclinical evidence supporting human observations.","The 'dual role' of P. bifermentans involves two different mechanisms (live bacteria for toxicity, metabolite for efficacy); ensure this distinction is clear when citing.","Clinical associations are based on retrospective/prospective cohorts with potential confounders; causality is established primarily through animal models, not clinical intervention."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Provides empirical evidence linking specific gut bacteria (P. bifermentans) to both irAE pathogenesis and enhanced ICI efficacy through distinct mechanisms (barrier disruption vs. metabolite secretion).","limits":"The exact nature of the active < 3 kDa metabolite and its precise immune mechanism remain unidentified. The study relies on a limited number of matched longitudinal samples and mouse models that may not fully recapitulate human ir-colitis complexity."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"Three independent cohorts of melanoma and NSCLC patients treated with ICI","finding":"Grade ≥ 2 irAEs are associated with significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival, even after adjusting for immortal time bias."},{"conditions":"Baseline stool samples from melanoma patients analyzed via shotgun metagenomics","finding":"Patients developing grade ≥ 2 irAEs exhibited lower alpha diversity and enrichment of pro-inflammatory taxa including Ruminococcus gnavus and Streptococcus vestibularis compared to those without irAEs."},{"conditions":"Stool samples from patients with ir-colitis analyzed via culturomics","finding":"Paraclostridium bifermentans was isolated and found to be enriched in patients with acute ir-colitis compared to baseline or non-ir-colitis controls."},{"conditions":"In vivo mouse models receiving FMT from ir-colitis patients","finding":"FMT induced surrogate markers of intestinal inflammation (increased Lcn-2 and LPS) and enhanced the anti-tumor efficacy of dual anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 therapy."},{"conditions":"In vitro Caco-2 monolayer co-culture with P. bifermentans","finding":"Live P. bifermentans disrupted epithelial barrier integrity (reduced ZO-1 and Occludin signals) and increased pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-1β); this effect was not observed with cell-free supernatant."},{"conditions":"In vivo murine tumor model with oral gavage of P. bifermentans derivatives","finding":"Oral administration of P. bifermentans enhanced anti-tumor response to dual ICI; this beneficial effect was retained by cell-free supernatant filtered to < 3 kDa, indicating mediation by a small-molecule metabolite rather than live bacteria."}],"problem_or_question":"The study aims to resolve the mechanism underlying the observed correlation between irAEs and improved ICI efficacy. Specifically, it seeks to determine if specific gut microbial signatures predict irAEs and efficacy, and to identify causal bacterial agents that might drive both inflammation and anti-tumor responses.","research_scope":"The study focuses on patients with advanced melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). It investigates the relationship between gut microbiome composition, the development of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), and clinical outcomes (overall survival and progression-free survival). The research combines clinical cohort analysis with shotgun metagenomics and culturomics to identify specific bacterial taxa and their functional roles."}

identity.title: Breakthroughs in immune checkpoint therapy: overcoming NSCLC immune checkpoint therapy resistance with novel techniques

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为理解肠道微生物群如何影响实体瘤ICI疗效提供了背景机制和潜在连接点。虽然其主要焦点是NSCLC，但其关于TME重塑、免疫监视以及克服耐药的综合论述，特别是专门章节讨论微生物组调节疗法，可直接用于回答微生物群如何调制ICI疗效及其介导机制的问题。它提供了从代谢产物（如丁酸盐）到特定受体轴（如PD-L2-RGMB）的具体作用路径描述。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该论文是综述性质，其关于微生物组机制的描述（如PD-L2-RGMB轴）是基于引用的研究，并非本综述作者原创的实验发现。","文中提到的临床试验结果（如SKYSCRAPER-01失败案例）提示单一靶点或简单组合可能无效，需谨慎推断微生物组疗法的普适性。","NSCLC是主要研究对象，虽然机制可能在其他实体瘤中保守，但外推至其他癌种时需考虑组织特异性差异。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了针对NSCLC中ICI耐药机制的系统性分类框架，区分了原发性和获得性耐药的具体分子路径。","limits":"作为综述，其结论依赖于所引用的文献质量；对于某些新兴策略（如特定微生物组疗法或AI模型），多为早期临床前或I/II期试验结果，缺乏大规模III期确证数据。"},{"contribution":"整合了多种克服耐药的技术路线，为后续研究提供了潜在的联合治疗靶点列表。","limits":"未能提供不同策略之间的直接比较数据，无法确定哪种单一策略最优。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"原发性耐药","finding":"涉及肿瘤内在因素（低TMB、MHC下调、cGAS-STING通路抑制、ADSL/NAT8L介导的代谢逃逸）和外在因素（TME中MDSCs/Tregs浸润、抑制性细胞因子分泌）。"},{"conditions":"获得性耐药","finding":"主要机制包括肿瘤抗原谱改变（抗原丢失）、干扰素信号通路缺陷（如JAK突变）、T细胞耗竭加深、以及TME中免疫抑制细胞招募增加。"},{"conditions":"克服策略","finding":"联合疗法（化疗诱导免疫原性死亡、放疗激活STING通路）、微生物组调节（短链脂肪酸、特定菌群轴）、个性化新抗原疫苗、表观遗传药物（HDACi/DNMTi）及AI辅助的生物标志物筛选被证明具有潜力。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管免疫检查点抑制剂改变了癌症治疗格局，但大量患者存在原发或获得性耐药，限制了其长期疗效。本研究旨在解析这些耐药机制，并综合评估新兴技术如何克服这些障碍以改善患者预后。","research_scope":"非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）及其他实体瘤中的免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）治疗，重点聚焦于原发性与获得性耐药机制及克服耐药的新技术。"}

identity.title: Immunological Drug–Drug Interactions in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Artificial Intelligence

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为理解肠道微生物群如何调节ICI疗效提供了详细的机制背景和临床证据汇总，特别是关于抗生素和PPIs的影响。它明确了微生物群介导的iDDIs是核心机制之一，并指出了当前证据的局限性（如混杂因素），这有助于在综述中定位微生物群研究的现状和挑战。同时，它提供的AI技术视角可作为讨论未来研究方向或方法学挑战的背景素材。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述主要关注固体肿瘤（如NSCLC, RCC, UC），结论外推至其他癌症类型需谨慎。","所有关于抗生素和PPIs的负面效应均源于观察性数据，存在显著的混杂偏倚风险，不应视为确凿的因果证据。","AI部分内容为技术综述，不代表已验证的临床工具，其实际效用尚不确定。","微生物群机制的描述基于现有文献的综合，具体菌株与特定ICI反应的因果关系在不同研究中可能不一致。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提出了iDDIs的概念框架，将伴随用药影响分为微生物群、全身免疫抑制和TME调节三类；系统总结了各类药物的临床证据和AI应用现状。","limits":"作为综述，依赖已发表的观察性研究和荟萃分析，因果推断受限；未提供新的原始实验数据；AI部分多为理论探讨和技术综述，缺乏实证结果。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"围ICI期使用抗生素或PPIs","finding":"多项荟萃分析显示与较差的总生存期（OS）和无进展生存期（PFS）相关，其中抗生素暴露于ICI启动前30-90天效果最强；存在“病人用户偏差”混杂。"},{"conditions":"皮质类固醇用于姑息治疗 vs. irAE管理","finding":"表现出“指征反转”现象：用于姑息治疗时与较差预后相关，而用于irAE管理时通常不损害生存；峰值剂量比累积暴露量更具预测性。"},{"conditions":"RAAS抑制剂（ACEi/ARBs）","finding":"部分回顾性研究显示可能改善OS，尤其在尿路上皮癌和肾细胞癌中，但证据来自观察性研究。"},{"conditions":"当前AI应用状态","finding":"处于早期阶段，多为概念验证；缺乏外部验证和标准化数据集；LLM存在幻觉风险；需结合多模态数据和前瞻性研究。"}],"problem_or_question":"传统药代动力学/药效学（PK/PD）框架无法充分解释伴随用药对ICI疗效的影响；需要理解iDDIs的系统级机制，并探索如何利用AI技术应对iDDIs的高维复杂性、时间动态性和情境依赖性。","research_scope":"免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）治疗中的免疫学药物-药物相互作用（iDDIs），涵盖抗生素、质子泵抑制剂（PPIs）、皮质类固醇、阿片类药物、苯二氮卓类药物以及心血管/代谢药物对ICI疗效和安全性的影响，并探讨人工智能（AI）在识别和管理这些相互作用中的应用。"}

identity.title: Bacteria in cancer therapy: A new generation of weapons

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为理解“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤中免疫检查点抑制剂的疗效”提供了重要的背景框架和机制线索。虽然其主要焦点是外源性细菌疗法，但其关于肠道共生菌（特别是双歧杆菌）增强DC功能、促进CD8+ T细胞浸润以及与PD-L1抗体协同作用的论述，直接关联到F1和F2两个子问题。它提供了从机制层面解释为何特定菌群存在会影响ICI疗效的理论基础。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述主要关注外源性细菌疗法（therapeutic bacteria），在引用其关于肠道菌群的内容时，需注意区分治疗性细菌应用与自然肠道共生菌群的差异。","文中提到的“共识”仅限于作者对领域现状的描述，实际临床中微生物标志物尚存争议，引用时需保留这种不确定性。","多数机制证据来自小鼠模型，直接推断至人类临床疗效时需考虑物种差异和临床转化的局限性。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"系统归纳了细菌介导肿瘤治疗的多种免疫机制，包括靶向微环境、炎症小体激活、TLR信号通路、代谢产物作用及免疫细胞调节。","limits":"所给摘要未交代具体的文献检索策略、纳入排除标准及质量评估方法，属于叙述性综述而非系统性综述。"},{"contribution":"明确了不同细菌菌株（沙门氏菌、双歧杆菌等）在机制上的差异及其与免疫检查点抑制剂的潜在协同作用。","limits":"大部分证据来自动物实验（小鼠模型），临床转化数据有限，仅提及BCG用于膀胱癌及少数正在进行或完成的临床试验，缺乏大规模人体临床结果的支持。"},{"contribution":"指出了细菌疗法面临的挑战（致病性、DNA不稳定性、半衰期短）及基因工程改造的未来方向。","limits":"对于肠道微生物群影响ICI疗效的具体分子机制描述较为宏观，未深入探讨所有队列研究中存在的异质性和矛盾结果。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"固体肿瘤缺氧/坏死微环境","finding":"专性厌氧菌（如梭菌、双歧杆菌）利用缺氧特性特异性定植；兼性厌氧菌（如沙门氏菌、李斯特菌）通过血管渗漏被动聚集或对肿瘤化合物趋化。"},{"conditions":"细菌成分与模式识别受体相互作用","finding":"细菌PAMPs（LPS、鞭毛蛋白、CpG-DNA）分别激活TLR4、TLR5、TLR9，通过MyD88依赖或非依赖途径诱导促炎因子（TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-γ）释放，桥接先天与适应性免疫。"},{"conditions":"细菌感染导致的细胞损伤","finding":"细菌引起的肿瘤细胞损伤释放ATP等DAMPs，激活巨噬细胞中的NLRP3炎症小体，促进IL-1β和IL-18成熟，导致肿瘤消退。"},{"conditions":"特定细菌菌株处理","finding":"沙门氏菌可下调PD-L1和IDO表达，抑制肿瘤血管生成；双歧杆菌可增强树突状细胞功能，促进CD8+ T细胞浸润，并与抗PD-L1抗体产生协同效应。"},{"conditions":"肠道微生物群与免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）联用","finding":"特定的肠道菌群（如双歧杆菌、某些厚壁菌门细菌）与ICIs疗效正相关，而抗生素使用可能削弱疗效；粪菌移植和活菌制剂正在临床试验中以改善ICI响应。"}],"problem_or_question":"解决传统癌症治疗（放疗、化疗）毒性大、难以渗透深层组织及易产生耐药性的问题；阐明细菌介导的抗肿瘤免疫治疗的具体机制，以便更好地将其与其他治疗手段整合。","research_scope":"细菌介导的肿瘤免疫治疗，重点在于其作用机制（特别是免疫机制），涉及多种细菌菌株（如沙门氏菌、双歧杆菌、梭菌等）与宿主免疫系统及肿瘤微环境的相互作用。"}

identity.title: Impact of Patient Characteristics on the Outcomes of Patients with Gastrointestinal Cancers Treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review provides detailed mechanistic explanations and clinical evidence regarding how patient-specific factors, particularly the gut microbiome and systemic inflammation, modulate ICI efficacy in solid tumors. It is highly relevant for explaining the biological plausibility behind microbiome-mediated ICI responses and identifying confounding physiological states (like sarcopenia or liver metastasis) that may impair immunotherapy.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review aggregates data from various GI cancer types; results for one type (e.g., HCC) may not apply to another (e.g., CRC).","Microbiome findings are largely correlational in humans; causal claims rely on animal models mentioned in the text.","Antibiotic association is time-dependent (30 vs 60 days); precise timing matters.","Many findings are from retrospective studies or subgroup analyses of RCTs, not prospective randomized trials designed specifically for these factors."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Provides a comprehensive synthesis of patient-related prognostic factors for ICI response in GI cancers, linking clinical subgroup analyses from major RCTs with underlying immunological mechanisms.","limits":"The review includes many retrospective studies which lack robustness for definitive conclusions. It is limited to demographic and easily measurable clinical variables, excluding others like smoking or ethnicity. The absence of formal meta-analyses means firm conclusions on variable significance across studies cannot be made. Several figures referenced are not readable."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"Age <65 vs ≥65 in CheckMate-577 and KEYNOTE-177; Age <70 vs ≥70 in KEYNOTE-177","finding":"Younger patients (<65 or <70 depending on trial) showed statistically significant OS benefits from ICI, whereas older patients did not reach statistical significance, though trends were often consistent. Differences may relate to tolerability rather than specific immunological mechanisms."},{"conditions":"Female vs Male across multiple GI cancer RCTs (KEYNOTE-590, CheckMate-577, CheckMate-649, HIMALAYA)","finding":"Females generally showed inferior or non-significant OS benefits compared to males in combination therapies. This is hypothesized to be due to stronger immune surveillance leading to more robust immune escape mechanisms in female tumors, higher autoimmune side effects, and lower tumor mutational burden in females."},{"conditions":"ECOG PS 0 vs 1 in CheckMate-649, IMbrave-150, TOPAZ-1, KEYNOTE-177","finding":"Results are inconsistent. Some trials showed better relative benefit for ECOG 1 over ECOG 0, possibly because ECOG 0 patients derive sufficient benefit from chemotherapy alone, masking the incremental ICI benefit. ECOG ≥2 is associated with poor outcomes based on retrospective data."},{"conditions":"Asian vs Non-Asian regions in HCC (COSMIC-312, HIMALAYA) and Biliary Tract Cancer (TOPAZ-1)","finding":"ICIs showed superior OS benefits in Asian regions compared to non-Asian regions. This is attributed to different etiologies: viral hepatitis (HBV/HCV) in Asia vs NASH/alcohol in non-Asia. NASH-related HCC exhibits dysfunctional/tired CTLs and fibrosis that limit ICI efficacy."},{"conditions":"BMI ≥25 vs <25 in advanced HCC and solid tumors","finding":"Higher BMI (obesity/overweight) is associated with improved OS, PFS, and objective response rates. Obesity creates a pro-inflammatory state with increased leukocyte counts and M1 macrophages, potentially enhancing anti-tumor immunity."},{"conditions":"Presence of Sarcopenia/Cachexia in Gastric and Liver Cancer","finding":"Sarcopenia is consistently associated with poor OS and worse ICI outcomes. Reduced muscle mass leads to reduced myokine production (e.g., IL-15) and chronic low-grade inflammation, contributing to an immunosuppressed state and CTL exhaustion."},{"conditions":"Gut Microbiome Composition and Antibiotic Use","finding":"Specific bacterial abundances (e.g., Lachnospiraceae, Bifidobacterium) correlate with better ICI outcomes, while others (Veillonellaceae) correlate with worse outcomes. Recent antibiotic use (within 30 days) before ICI initiation is associated with significantly worse OS, likely due to microbiome disruption."},{"conditions":"Liver Metastases in Esophagogastric and Pan-cancer cohorts","finding":"Liver metastases are associated with significantly shorter OS and PFS. The liver microenvironment is immunosuppressive, sequestering CTLs and promoting Treg function. However, some pan-cancer data suggests this negative effect might be mitigated when ICIs are combined with other modalities like radiation or CTLA-4 inhibitors."},{"conditions":"Peritoneal Metastases with Ascites in MSI-H Colorectal Cancer","finding":"Peritoneal metastases alone do not necessarily predict poor ICI response, but the presence of ascites is strongly associated with significantly reduced PFS and OS. Peritoneal metastases have distinct immune profiles (higher M2 macrophages, VEGF)."}],"problem_or_question":"While molecular factors like PD-L1 expression and MSI status are well-studied predictors of ICI response, there is a need to understand how broader patient-related factors (demographics, physiology, comorbidities, and microbiome) modulate ICI efficacy in GI cancers. The review aims to identify these factors and explore their immunological basis to improve patient selection and outcome prediction.","research_scope":"The review focuses on gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, specifically esophageal, gastric, colorectal, hepatocellular, pancreatic, and biliary tract cancers. It examines patient-related prognostic factors influencing the response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy."}

identity.title: Role of the intestinal microbiome and microbial-derived metabolites in immune checkpoint blockade immunotherapy of cancer

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review provides a comprehensive overview of the gut microbiome's influence on ICI efficacy and toxicity in solid tumors. It is valuable for establishing the current state of knowledge regarding which microbes and metabolites are implicated, the proposed mechanisms (antigen-dependent/independent), and the clinical implications of antibiotic use and FMT. It serves as a foundational text for discussing the 'how' and 'why' of microbiome modulation in ICI therapy, while also highlighting the limitations and inconsistencies that characterize the field.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review covers both preclinical (mouse) and clinical (human) data; distinctions must be maintained when attributing findings to human applicability.","Identified bacterial taxa and metabolites show inconsistency across studies; do not present them as universal predictors without noting context-dependence (tumor type, geography, methodology).","Mechanistic explanations (especially antigen mimicry) are presented as emerging hypotheses supported by limited evidence; avoid overstating their generalizability.","FMT efficacy is based on very small pilot studies; conclusions about its therapeutic potential are preliminary and controversial."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Synthesizes fragmented preclinical and clinical evidence into a coherent framework distinguishing antigen-dependent and antigen-independent mechanisms of microbiome-ICI interaction.","limits":"The review acknowledges significant inconsistency in identified bacterial taxa across studies due to technical heterogeneity, population differences, and tumor type specificity; it does not resolve these discrepancies but highlights them as areas needing larger standardized studies."},{"contribution":"Identifies specific metabolites (SCFAs, tryptophan derivatives, inosine) and their associations with ICI outcomes, providing a basis for metabolic biomarker development.","limits":"Most metabolite data come from small cohort studies or single centers; causal relationships and reproducibility across diverse populations remain unconfirmed."},{"contribution":"Highlights the potential of FMT as a therapeutic strategy to overcome ICI resistance and treat colitis, based on early-phase clinical trials.","limits":"Current FMT evidence is limited to small case series and pilot studies; safety, optimal donor selection, and long-term efficacy are not yet established."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"Preclinical mouse models (SPF vs GF, antibiotic treatment)","finding":"Intact commensal microbiome is required for anti-tumor efficacy of anti-CTLA-4 antibodies; germ-free or antibiotic-depleted mice show compromised responses."},{"conditions":"Human metastatic melanoma patients treated with anti-CTLA-4","finding":"Higher abundance of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Gemmiger formicilis associated with positive response; Bacteroides associated with poor response."},{"conditions":"Human advanced NSCLC or urothelial carcinomas treated with ICIs","finding":"Increased relative abundances of Akkermansia muciniphila and Enterococcus hirae associated with clinical response."},{"conditions":"Human solid tumors treated with anti-PD-1","finding":"Higher fecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), particularly propionate, associated with longer progression-free survival in some cohorts, though conflicting results exist for butyrate and other SCFAs across different cohorts."},{"conditions":"Patients receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics prior to or during ICI therapy","finding":"Antibiotic use is consistently associated with reduced ICI efficacy, shorter overall survival, and shorter progression-free survival."},{"conditions":"ICI-associated colitis pathogenesis","finding":"Specific bacteria (e.g., Bacteroides fragilis, Burkholderia cepacia) may protect against colitis by promoting regulatory T cells; conversely, increases in Firmicutes have been linked to higher incidence of colitis."},{"conditions":"Mechanistic pathways","finding":"Two major mechanisms identified: (1) Antigen-independent: Microbes modulate innate/adaptive immunity (e.g., dendritic cell activation, CD8+ T cell infiltration); (2) Antigen-specific: Molecular mimicry where microbial epitopes cross-react with tumor neoantigens."}],"problem_or_question":"How does the intestinal microbiome modulate the efficacy and toxicity of ICIs? What are the specific microbial signatures and mechanisms involved, and how can these insights be translated into clinical biomarkers or therapies?","research_scope":"The review focuses on the role of the intestinal microbiome and microbial-derived metabolites in modulating responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in cancer patients, specifically addressing efficacy outcomes (tumor response, survival) and toxicities (immune-related adverse events like colitis). It covers preclinical mouse models and retrospective/prospective human clinical studies."}

identity.title: Predictive impact of sarcopenia in solid cancers treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a meta‐analysis

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"本文提供了肌少症（肌肉量/质下降）作为ICI疗效预测因子的宏观流行病学证据。虽然不直接涉及肠道菌群，但其提出的“肌源性细胞因子（myokines）”机制假说（如IL-15调节T细胞/NK细胞）为理解宿主全身状态如何影响免疫治疗提供了重要的生物学背景线索，可作为解释“宿主微环境/系统性因素”调节ICI效应的参考框架。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["本文是荟萃分析，提供的是统计关联而非因果证明。肌少症可能是疾病严重程度或营养不良的标志，而非直接的致病原因。","不同研究使用的肌少症切值（cut-off values）差异较大，且多数研究未充分调整BMI、体能状态等混杂因素，解读效应大小时需谨慎。","存在显著的发表偏倚，阳性结果可能被高估。","虽然提到了IL-15机制，但这属于作者引用的其他研究或动物实验，本论文本身并未测量这些分子指标。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了肌少症作为ICI疗效负向预测因子的综合证据，证实其在多种实体瘤中的普遍性；比较了不同CT影像指标（SMI, PMI, SMD）的预测一致性。","limits":"所给摘要未交代具体的异质性来源细节；纳入研究多为回顾性设计，存在混杂因素调整不足的风险；存在显著的发表偏倚；无法确定因果机制，仅能提供关联证据。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"所有纳入的26项研究（n=2501），总体人群","finding":"肌少症患病率为44.7%。肌少症与较差的OS（HR=1.55, 95% CI: 1.32–1.82）和PFS（HR=1.61, 95% CI: 1.35–1.93）显著相关。"},{"conditions":"总体人群","finding":"肌少症患者出现较差的放射学反应：ORR降低（OR=0.52, 95% CI: 0.34–0.80）和DCR降低（OR=0.45, 95% CI: 0.30–0.67）。"},{"conditions":"按诊断指标分层","finding":"SMI和PMI均能预测OS和PFS，其中PMI在OS预测上因统计效能不足未达显著性（HR=1.97, 95% CI: 0.88–4.41），但在PFS上显著（HR=1.86, 95% CI: 1.08–3.21）。SMD在OS和PFS预测上均未达到统计学显著性（OS HR=1.41, PFS HR=1.27）。不同诊断指标间差异无统计学意义。"},{"conditions":"亚组分析：黑色素瘤和NSCLC","finding":"在这两种主要肿瘤类型中，肌少症与较差的OS、PFS和DCR的关联与总体结果一致且具有统计学显著性。"},{"conditions":"总体人群","finding":"肌少症与严重毒性（severe toxicity）的发生无显著关联（OR=1.13, 95% CI: 0.51–2.52）。"}],"problem_or_question":"解决既往研究中关于肌少症是否影响ICI疗效的矛盾结果，明确肌少症作为ICI疗效预测生物标志物的价值，并比较不同肌少症诊断指标（如SMI、PMI、SMD）的预测效能差异。","research_scope":"实体瘤患者接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）治疗的情况；关注肌少症（sarcopenia）状态与ICI疗效及毒性的关联。"}

identity.title: Gut microbiota's role in NAFLD- and HBV/HCV-related hepatocellular carcinoma: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications.

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述提供了肠道微生物群影响肝细胞癌（HCC）的基础机制背景，特别是关于炎症、代谢和免疫调节的共同通路。虽然其主要焦点是HCC而非直接针对免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）的疗效，但其关于微生物群调节免疫监视（特别是在HBV/HCV背景下）以及免疫抑制微环境的论述，可为解释微生物群如何间接影响抗肿瘤免疫反应提供理论框架。此外，文中提到的后生元（如短链脂肪酸）的抗炎和促凋亡作用，可作为微生物代谢产物调节肿瘤微环境的实例素材。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该论文为综述性质，其结论依赖于被引用的原始研究，摘要未提供独立的实验数据。","论文主要关注HCC，而用户关注的核心问题是ICIs在固体瘤中的疗效，需注意疾病模型和治疗场景的差异。","文中提到的“免疫监视”和“免疫抑制微环境”是基础机制描述，不能直接外推为对ICI疗效的具体预测指标。","所给材料未交代具体的文献检索策略，因此无法评估其综述的全面性和偏倚风险。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了NAFLD和病毒性肝炎相关HCC中肠道微生物群作用的比较视角，归纳了共同的分子机制（LPS-TLR4、胆汁酸、免疫抑制）。","limits":"所给摘要未交代具体的文献检索范围、纳入排除标准及证据质量评估方法；未提供针对免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）疗效的具体数据或机制分析。"},{"contribution":"总结了多种微生物靶向治疗策略（益生菌、后生元、FMT）在HCC中的潜在应用。","limits":"治疗潜力的描述较为概括，未提供具体的临床试验结果、剂量效应或长期安全性数据；对于“有效未来策略”的断言属于作者观点，尚需更多验证。"},{"contribution":"明确了当前研究的局限性，包括因果性缺失、肝内转移机制不明及多界微生物组研究的不足。","limits":"这些局限性是作者提出的建议，而非本综述本身解决的结果；对于真菌组和病毒组的具体发现，摘要仅指出其未被充分研究。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"NAFLD-related HCC","finding":"微生物群组成的改变促进了肠道屏障功能障碍、内毒素血症和代谢紊乱。"},{"conditions":"HBV/HCV-related HCC","finding":"微生物组调节免疫监视和病毒持续性。"},{"conditions":"Shared pathogenic pathways","finding":"LPS-TLR4信号通路、胆汁酸失调和免疫抑制微环境是跨病因的共享致病途径。"},{"conditions":"Therapeutic interventions","finding":"抗生素、饮食、益生菌和后生元（如短链脂肪酸、戊酸）具有抗炎和促凋亡作用；粪便微生物移植和饮食调节显示出改善预后的潜力。"},{"conditions":"Research gaps","finding":"目前缺乏因果关系的建立、对肝内转移的理解以及对真菌组（mycobiome）和病毒组（virome）角色的调查。"}],"problem_or_question":"1. 肠道微生物群失调如何具体参与NAFLD相关和病毒性肝炎相关HCC的发病机制？2. 不同病因的HCC是否存在共享的微生物致病通路？3. 基于微生物群的干预措施在HCC的预防和治疗中具有何种潜力？4. 当前该领域存在哪些关键的研究空白？","research_scope":"肝细胞癌（HCC），特别是与非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）相关的HCC以及与乙型肝炎病毒（HBV）/丙型肝炎病毒（HCV）相关的HCC。研究聚焦于肠道微生物群在“肠-肝轴”病理生理中的作用，涵盖机制、治疗潜力及未来研究方向。"}

identity.title: The role of the gut microbiome in modulating immunotherapy efficacy in colorectal cancer

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为理解肠道微生物群如何调节结直肠癌免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）疗效提供了全面的机制框架和临床背景。它特别适用于回答“微生物群如何影响ICI疗效”及其“介导机制”的问题，提供了从分子机制（代谢物、信号通路）到临床表型（响应率、副作用）的多层次证据。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该综述主要针对结直肠癌，其结论不能直接外推到其他实体瘤，尽管机制可能有相似之处。","所引用的临床试验多为早期阶段，疗效证据等级有限，需谨慎解读其临床转化意义。","微生物群的分析方法和结果报告在不同研究中存在异质性，跨研究比较时需考虑技术差异。","作者声称的“系统性综述和荟萃分析”在提供的文本中未展示详细的检索策略、纳入排除标准及定量合并统计结果，因此其“荟萃分析”部分的严谨性和透明度有待原文进一步确认。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"系统总结了肠道微生物群影响结直肠癌ICI疗效的多重机制，包括免疫细胞调节、代谢物作用和信号通路调控。","limits":"作为综述，其结论依赖于所纳入研究的原始数据质量；部分机制（如具体菌株的因果效应）仍主要基于观察性研究或动物模型，临床转化证据尚不充分。"},{"contribution":"指出了通过FMT、益生菌和饮食调整操纵肠道微生物群作为辅助治疗策略的潜力。","limits":"所引用的临床试验多为早期阶段（如Phase I/II）或小样本研究，缺乏大规模长期随访数据支持其普遍有效性。"},{"contribution":"明确了微生物多样性及特定菌属丰度作为预测ICI疗效的生物标志物的可能性。","limits":"不同研究间使用的测序方法、数据分析流程和临床终点定义可能存在异质性，限制了跨研究的直接比较。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"结直肠癌患者接受PD-1/PD-L1或CTLA-4抑制剂治疗","finding":"肠道微生物群的组成和多样性与ICI疗效显著相关。富含某些有益菌（如Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Akkermansia muciniphila）的患者通常对治疗反应更好；而某些致病菌（如Enterobacteriaceae）的过度生长与较差的预后相关。"},{"conditions":"机制层面：代谢物与免疫调节","finding":"特定细菌产生的代谢物（如短链脂肪酸SCFAs，特别是丁酸和丙酸）能抑制炎症通路（如NF-κB），增强CD8+ T细胞的抗肿瘤活性，并促进树突状细胞成熟。"},{"conditions":"干预措施：FMT与益生菌","finding":"粪便微生物移植（FMT）和特定益生菌补充（如YIT0132, GEN-001）在初步研究中显示出改善免疫微环境、减轻ICI副作用（如结肠炎）并可能提高治疗反应的潜力。"}],"problem_or_question":"肠道微生物群如何调节结直肠癌免疫治疗的疗效？其背后的生物学机制是什么？以及如何通过操纵肠道微生物群来优化治疗效果？","research_scope":"结直肠癌（Colorectal Cancer, CRC）患者中肠道微生物群与免疫治疗（特别是免疫检查点抑制剂，ICIs）疗效之间的关系。涵盖机制、临床关联及干预策略。"}

identity.title: Microbiota: A key factor affecting and regulating the efficacy of immunotherapy

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该综述为理解肠道微生物群如何调节免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）在实体瘤中的疗效提供了宏观的理论框架和机制线索。它不直接提供新的实验数据，而是整合了现有的证据，特别指出了“微生物-宿主信号传导”和“微生物向肿瘤易位”两个关键机制维度，以及“调节微生物群”作为联合治疗策略的临床潜力。这对于构建综述中关于机制解释和治疗干预部分的素材具有参考价值。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该论文为综述性质，其结论依赖于其所引用的原始研究的质量和数据一致性。阅读时需区分作者的综合观点与各原始研究的独立发现。","摘要中提到的“微生物易位”和“信号传导”是机制假设或观察到的现象关联，具体分子机制需参考其他提供详细实验证据的论文。","该综述未限定特定的癌症类型或ICIs种类，因此在应用于具体实体瘤或特定药物（如PD-1/PD-L1 vs CTLA-4）的细分问题时，需谨慎外推，最好寻找针对特定亚组的综述或实证研究进行补充。","所给材料未提供具体的文献检索数据库、时间范围或筛选标准，因此其覆盖的全面性和代表性存在不确定性。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了关于微生物群如何影响免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）疗效的综合视角，特别强调了微生物-宿主信号传导和微生物易位这两个具体机制路径。","limits":"所给摘要未交代具体的文献检索策略、纳入/排除标准及质量评价方法。由于仅基于摘要和片段，无法确认其是否涵盖了所有类型的免疫治疗药物或所有主要癌症亚型的具体数据对比。对于“微生物易位”等机制的描述停留在概念层面，缺乏具体的分子通路细节或定量证据支持。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"基于现有文献的综合分析","finding":"微生物群不仅直接影响癌症发展，还在免疫治疗中发挥重要作用。不同微生物群通过信号改变肿瘤微环境，进而影响免疫治疗疗效。"},{"conditions":"机制层面","finding":"微生物-宿主信号传导和微生物向肿瘤的易位是影响免疫治疗反应的关键机制。"},{"conditions":"临床应用层面","finding":"调节微生物群是一种有潜力的联合免疫治疗新策略，但其给药方式和临床转化仍需进一步细化和探索。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管免疫治疗是癌症治疗的重大突破，但患者响应率有限且存在副作用，缺乏有效的预测标志物。本研究旨在解决如何通过理解微生物群的作用来增强免疫治疗效果，并探索调节微生物群作为辅助治疗手段的潜力。","research_scope":"肿瘤免疫治疗（特别是免疫检查点抑制剂，ICIs）与宿主微生物群（包括肠道菌群及肠外微生物）之间的相互作用。研究对象涵盖细菌、古菌、噬菌体、真核病毒和真菌等微生物组成，以及它们对癌症发展和免疫治疗反应的影响。"}

identity.title: The gut microbiome in lung cancer: from pathogenesis to precision therapy

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review serves as a foundational resource for understanding the gut-lung axis in lung cancer, particularly its impact on immunotherapy efficacy. It provides detailed descriptions of microbial signatures associated with ICI response, mechanistic pathways involving metabolites and immune cells, and emerging therapeutic strategies. It is highly relevant for facets concerning how the microbiome modulates ICI efficacy and the underlying mechanisms.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review is a narrative synthesis, not a systematic review or meta-analysis; therefore, it does not provide pooled effect sizes or rigorous statistical aggregation of all available evidence.","Many mechanistic claims are based on preclinical (mouse) models or correlative clinical studies; causal relationships in humans are not definitively proven within this text.","The term 'solid tumours' in the user's plan is broader than the paper's primary focus on lung cancer; users must extrapolate carefully when applying lung-specific findings to other solid tumors."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Provides a comprehensive overview of the gut-lung axis in lung cancer, linking specific microbial taxa and metabolites to clinical outcomes in diagnosis and immunotherapy.","limits":"As a narrative review, it does not present new primary data or perform a systematic meta-analysis. The causal relationships described are largely inferred from correlative clinical studies and preclinical models, which may vary across populations."},{"contribution":"Identifies specific microbial signatures (e.g., A. muciniphila, SCFA producers) and metabolic profiles as potential biomarkers for predicting ICI response.","limits":"The generalizability of these biomarkers depends on the heterogeneity of patient cohorts and sequencing methodologies used in the cited studies, which are not standardized in this review."},{"contribution":"Discusses therapeutic interventions like FMT and probiotics as adjuncts to cancer therapy, highlighting their potential to overcome resistance.","limits":"Clinical translation faces challenges including interindividual variability, lack of standardized protocols for FMT/probiotics, and long-term safety concerns, which are noted but not resolved."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"In lung cancer patients compared to healthy controls","finding":"Patients exhibit dysbiosis characterized by increased abundance of Ruminococcus, Enterobacteriaceae, Lachnospiraceae, and decreased levels of Faecalibacterium, Bifidobacterium, and Veillonella. Metabolic profiles show reduced SCFA production and increased lactate."},{"conditions":"For early detection of lung cancer","finding":"A panel of 13 microbial biomarkers was identified with high diagnostic potential, achieving an AUC of 92.4% in discovery and 67.7% in validation cohorts using a Patient Discrimination Index (PDI)."},{"conditions":"Predicting response to Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs)","finding":"Baseline presence of Akkermansia muciniphila, Faecalibacterium spp., and Clostridiales correlates with improved ICI outcomes. Higher levels of acetate, propionate, and butyrate are associated with prolonged progression-free survival. A TOPOSCORE integrating species interaction groups and A. muciniphila abundance predicts individual responses."},{"conditions":"Impact of antibiotics and probiotics on ICI efficacy","finding":"Antibiotic use prior to ICI therapy is associated with reduced overall survival and impaired efficacy. Probiotic supplementation (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Clostridium butyricum) may enhance ICI efficacy and improve survival outcomes in NSCLC patients."},{"conditions":"Mechanisms of action","finding":"Gut microbes modulate lung immunity via metabolites (SCFAs), antigen presentation, and immune cell trafficking. Specific bacteria like A. muciniphila can translocate to tumor tissues, restructure the intratumoral ecosystem, and restore exhausted CD8+ T cells, enhancing anti-PD-1 therapy efficacy."}],"problem_or_question":"To synthesize existing evidence regarding how the gut microbiome influences lung cancer pathogenesis and treatment efficacy, particularly in the context of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), and to identify potential therapeutic strategies and biomarkers derived from this interaction.","research_scope":"The review focuses on the gut-lung axis in the context of lung cancer, specifically examining non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) and small cell lung carcinoma. It covers pathogenesis, early detection biomarkers, mechanisms of immune modulation, and therapeutic interventions including immunotherapy response prediction and microbiota-targeted treatments."}

identity.title: Gut microbial signatures and immunotherapy outcomes in NSCLC and melanoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文为综述F1（微生物组如何调节ICI疗效）提供了关键的定量综合证据，证实了肠道微生物组特征（多样性、特定菌属）与NSCLC和黑色素瘤患者ICI临床结局（生存、响应）的显著预后关联，并指出了抗生素使用的负面影响。同时，它为F2（机制）提供了部分支持性背景，讨论了特定菌属（如Akkermansia, Faecalibacterium）可能的免疫调节功能（T细胞招募、短链脂肪酸产生），但主要贡献在于表型关联而非机制验证。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该研究结论仅限于NSCLC和黑色素瘤，不能直接外推到其他实体瘤或血液肿瘤。","发现的关联是预后的，不等于预测性的；即微生物组特征与结局相关，但不一定特异性地预测ICI相对于其他治疗的额外获益。","证据确定性为“中等”，主要受限于观察性研究设计和结果异质性，解读时应保持谨慎，避免过度强调因果性。","对于irAEs，仅抗CTLA-4诱导的结肠炎有明确的定量保护关联证据，其他irAEs（尤其是抗PD-1相关）的证据不足或矛盾，不宜泛化。","机制解释是作者基于文献的推测，并非本综述的直接发现，引用时需明确区分关联证据和机制假说。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了关于肠道微生物组特征（多样性、特定菌属）与NSCLC和黑色素瘤患者ICI疗效及安全性之间关联的综合定量证据。确认了高多样性、Akkermansia、Faecalibacterium的有益关联以及抗生素使用的有害关联。区分了不同ICI类型（抗CTLA-4 vs. 抗PD-1）在irAEs方面的不同微生物关联。","limits":"纳入的研究均为观察性研究，无法确立因果关系。证据确定性被评定为“中等”，主要因研究设计的观察性质和部分结果的不一致性。由于原始数据不可用，无法进行个体参与者数据（IPD）分析，限制了更精细的混杂因素调整。术语上只能界定为“预后”关联，难以严格区分“预测”价值。对于抗PD-1/PD-L1治疗相关的irAEs，因数据异质性过大，未能进行荟萃分析。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"基线高肠道微生物α多样性 vs. 低多样性","finding":"显著改善OS (pooled HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.41–0.66) 和 PFS (pooled HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.47–0.71)。在NSCLC和黑色素瘤亚组中均稳健，且不受测序方法（16S vs. 宏基因组）影响。"},{"conditions":"基线存在 Akkermansia","finding":"显著增加客观缓解率 (ORR) (pooled OR 2.15, 95% CI 1.38–3.35)。"},{"conditions":"基线高丰度 Faecalibacterium","finding":"显著改善无进展生存期 (PFS) (pooled HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.54–0.85)。"},{"conditions":"ICI治疗前1-2个月内使用抗生素","finding":"显著恶化总生存期 (OS) (pooled HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.34–2.21)。"},{"conditions":"黑色素瘤患者接受抗CTLA-4治疗，基线高丰度 Bacteroidetes","finding":"显著降低严重（≥3级）结肠炎风险 (pooled OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.18–0.64)。"},{"conditions":"黑色素瘤患者接受抗CTLA-4治疗，基线高丰度 Bacteroides intestinalis","finding":"一项研究提示与严重毒性风险增加相关（未纳入荟萃分析）。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管已有证据表明肠道微生物组影响ICI疗效，但现有证据碎片化且存在不一致。本研究旨在定量综合基线肠道微生物组特征（多样性和特定菌属）与NSCLC和黑色素瘤患者ICI临床结局（生存、响应、不良反应）之间的关联，并评估证据质量，以明确其作为预后生物标志物的潜力。","research_scope":"非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）和黑色素瘤患者；接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs，包括抗PD-1/PD-L1或抗CTLA-4治疗）；基线肠道微生物组特征与临床结局（OS, PFS, ORR, irAEs）的关联。"}

identity.title: Impact of Periodontal Host-Modulation Therapies on Oral–Gut Microbiome Axis in Periodontitis Patients with Hematological Diseases: A Narrative Review

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文虽聚焦于血液系统恶性肿瘤而非实体瘤，但其关于“免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）通过口-肠轴影响全身免疫稳态”的机制论述，以及“口腔/肠道菌群失调如何调节免疫治疗相关毒性和潜在疗效”的理论框架，可为综述提供重要的病理生理学背景。特别是其关于牙龈卟啉单胞菌等病原体通过口-肠轴迁移并引发全身炎症的描述，可作为理解微生物组介导免疫治疗效应的案例参考。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["本文研究对象为血液系统恶性肿瘤患者，其免疫缺陷程度和治疗方案与实体瘤患者存在显著差异，因此其关于微生物组变化和免疫治疗反应的发现不能直接外推至实体瘤人群。","文中关于口-肠轴影响的论述多基于机制推测和小规模研究，尚未形成确凿的临床因果关系证据，使用时应视为假设性或探索性内容。","作者声称某些疗法（如SDD、Omega-3）具有全身性抗炎益处，但具体对免疫治疗疗效的最终影响（正面或负面）在本文中并未给出定论，仅为潜在可能性。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"构建了免疫治疗、牙周炎与口-肠轴之间的病理生理联系框架，特别强调了血液病患者的特殊性。","limits":"所给摘要未交代具体的统计合并结果或定量效应值；主要基于机制推论和小样本观察性研究的定性综合，因果推断能力有限。"},{"contribution":"提供了针对免疫抑制人群的具体临床管理建议，区分了不同宿主调节疗法的适用场景和风险。","limits":"缺乏大规模随机对照试验的直接证据支持所述疗法的优越性；多数推荐基于专家共识或间接证据。"},{"contribution":"明确了口-肠轴在连接局部牙周感染与全身免疫治疗毒性/疗效中的潜在中介作用。","limits":"对于特定免疫药物（如BTK抑制剂、JAK抑制剂）对微生物组的具体影响，文中仅提及可能性，缺乏详细数据支撑。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"接受免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）或CAR-T治疗的血液系统恶性肿瘤患者","finding":"免疫治疗不仅增强抗肿瘤免疫，还可能导致免疫失调，加剧牙周炎症，加速附着丧失和骨吸收，并引起口腔菌群失调（机会性病原体增多，共生菌减少）。"},{"conditions":"存在牙周炎的免疫抑制患者","finding":"牙周炎作为慢性炎症源，可通过口-肠轴将病原菌（如牙龈卟啉单胞菌）及其代谢产物转运至肠道，导致肠道菌群失调、屏障功能受损（肠漏）和全身低度炎症，可能干扰造血微环境并降低免疫治疗疗效。"},{"conditions":"使用宿主调节疗法（SDD, Omega-3）","finding":"亚抗菌剂量多西环素（SDD）通过抑制基质金属蛋白酶（MMPs）减轻组织破坏而不扰乱菌群；Omega-3脂肪酸促进特异性促消退介质（SPMs）生成，主动解决炎症并保护黏膜屏障，两者均有助于在不抑制整体免疫的前提下控制局部和全身炎症。"},{"conditions":"使用微生物组靶向策略（益生菌、益生元）","finding":"可竞争性抑制致病菌、增强黏膜屏障并调节免疫反应。但在严重免疫抑制（如中性粒细胞缺乏）患者中需慎用活体益生菌，建议优先选择后生元或益生元以避免感染风险。"}],"problem_or_question":"探究免疫治疗（特别是针对血液系统恶性肿瘤）如何影响患者的牙周组织健康及口腔/肠道微生物组的组成与功能；评估宿主调节和微生物组靶向疗法在缓解免疫相关不良反应、稳定微生态和改善全身炎症状态中的潜在价值。","research_scope":"血液系统恶性肿瘤（如白血病、淋巴瘤、多发性骨髓瘤）患者，特别是接受免疫治疗（包括免疫检查点抑制剂ICIs和CAR-T细胞疗法）的人群。研究聚焦于牙周炎、口腔微生物组与肠道微生物组之间的相互作用（口-肠轴），以及宿主调节疗法和微生物组靶向干预在其中的应用。"}

identity.title: [Intestinal microbiom modulates the response to antitumor immunotherapy].

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review serves as a foundational source for understanding the general landscape of gut microbiome-immunotherapy interactions. It provides specific examples of bacterial taxa associated with response/non-response in melanoma, lung, and kidney cancers, details the mechanism of ICI resistance, and outlines the negative impact of antibiotics. It is valuable for establishing the context of microbiome modulation but explicitly notes the lack of consistent biomarkers, which helps frame discussions on variability and standardization needs.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review emphasizes that microbial associations are highly heterogeneous and not universally replicated. Do not treat any single taxon as a definitive diagnostic marker without acknowledging this variability.","Mechanistic insights are often extrapolated from mouse models (germ-free mice colonization) to humans. Caution is needed when applying these mechanisms directly to human clinical contexts.","The review is a narrative synthesis, not a systematic review with strict inclusion/exclusion criteria or meta-analytic statistics. Its findings represent the state of the field at the time of writing (2020) and should be contextualized within subsequent developments if available."]}

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文虽聚焦于口腔鳞状细胞癌（SCC）而非直接研究肠道微生物组与免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs），但其核心逻辑——即肿瘤微环境/局部微生物组通过调节宿主免疫因子（如DMBT1）进而影响治疗反应——为综述提供了重要的旁证和机制类比素材。它展示了实体瘤治疗（化疗放疗）中微生物组作为预后因子的潜力，以及宿主-微生物互作在调节治疗结局中的作用。对于综述而言，此文可作为“非肠道微生物组在实体瘤治疗反应中的作用”或“宿主免疫蛋白介导的微生物-治疗反应关联”的案例，补充关于局部微环境（口腔）而非全身肠道微生物组的证据，并提示DMBT1等分子可能作为连接微生物与宿主免疫反应的潜在桥梁。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["本文研究的是口腔鳞状细胞癌（SCC）的化疗放疗反应，而非黑色素瘤或其他实体瘤的免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）反应。因此，其发现的微生物标志物（如Gemella, Prevotella）不能直接外推至ICIs疗效预测。","DMBT1是一种唾液抗菌蛋白，主要参与先天免疫和病原体凝集，与ICIs作用的适应性免疫通路（PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4）不同。将其机制直接套用于ICIs需谨慎，应视为不同的免疫调节路径。","研究样本量有限（特别是配对样本和长期随访数据），且为单中心研究，结果的普适性有待验证。","微生物组与治疗反应的关联多为观察性，未排除混杂因素（如抗生素使用、口腔卫生状况等）的潜在影响。"]}

identity.title: The Role of the Gut Microbiome in Cancer Immunotherapy: Current Knowledge and Future Directions

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review serves as a foundational resource for understanding the mechanistic links and clinical correlations between gut microbiota and ICI efficacy in solid tumors. It provides a curated list of specific bacterial taxa and metabolites associated with response/resistance, outlines the biological pathways involved (e.g., T-cell activation, Treg suppression), and highlights the current state of interventional strategies (FMT, diet, probiotics). It is particularly useful for establishing the 'mechanism' facet and identifying key variables for the 'efficacy' facet, while also providing critical context on the limitations and heterogeneity of current evidence.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The review covers multiple solid tumor types, but most detailed clinical data are for melanoma and NSCLC. Findings may not generalize to all solid tumors.","Conflicting results for certain bacterial genera (e.g., *Bacteroides*) are highlighted; do not assume a single direction of effect without specifying the context (species, ICI type, patient cohort).","Mechanistic insights are often based on preclinical models; distinguish between proven human mechanisms and hypothesized pathways supported by animal data.","Interventional strategies (FMT, probiotics) are largely investigational; avoid presenting them as standard of care."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Provides a structured synthesis of the complex relationship between gut microbiota and ICI efficacy, categorizing mechanisms (metabolite-mediated, immune modulation) and summarizing clinical correlations across multiple tumor types.","limits":"As a narrative review, it does not perform a systematic meta-analysis with statistical pooling. The field is characterized by high heterogeneity and conflicting results, which the review acknowledges but cannot fully resolve due to the nature of the included studies."},{"contribution":"Identifies critical methodological pitfalls in current microbiome research, such as sample handling inconsistencies, lack of strain-level resolution, and uncontrolled confounders (diet, antibiotics), offering a roadmap for improving future study design.","limits":"The recommendations for future research are prospective; the review itself relies on existing data which may be biased by publication or selection effects common in early-stage microbiome studies."}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"In melanoma and NSCLC patients treated with ICIs","finding":"Specific bacterial taxa are correlated with ICI response, but results are often conflicting. Generally, higher alpha-diversity and abundance of certain commensals like *Bifidobacterium*, *Faecalibacterium prausnitzii*, and *Akkermansia muciniphila* are associated with better responses and prolonged progression-free survival (PFS). Conversely, some studies link *Bacteroides* species to either positive or negative outcomes depending on the specific species and ICI type."},{"conditions":"Preclinical and mechanistic studies","finding":"Gut microbiota modulate immunity via metabolites (e.g., short-chain fatty acids, inosine) and surface molecules (e.g., LPS, PSA). For instance, *B. pseudolongum* produces inosine which enhances T-cell activation via A2AR signaling, and *A. muciniphila* can induce pro-inflammatory cytokines and suppress Tregs, thereby enhancing anti-tumor immunity."},{"conditions":"Clinical intervention studies","finding":"Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) from responders to non-responders has shown promise in augmenting ICI efficacy in subsets of melanoma patients. Dietary interventions rich in fiber and probiotic supplementation are being investigated in ongoing trials to improve outcomes."}],"problem_or_question":"The review addresses the problem that a significant proportion of patients with solid tumors exhibit primary or acquired resistance to ICIs. It seeks to understand the role of the gut microbiome in this resistance and response variability, aiming to identify microbial signatures associated with therapeutic success and adverse events, and to evaluate potential microbiome-based interventions to improve clinical outcomes.","research_scope":"The review focuses on the interaction between the gut microbiome and the host immune system, specifically in the context of cancer immunotherapy using Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs). source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文为综述提供了关于微生物代谢物（IAA）通过 AhR 通路调控实体瘤免疫微环境的具体分子机制证据。它展示了工程菌作为局部药物递送平台，如何通过改变细胞因子谱（如 CXCL9/IFN-γ 升高，IL-17A 降低）来增强适应性免疫反应，为解释微生物如何影响免疫治疗响应提供了具体的机制案例。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该研究使用的是高免疫原性的结直肠癌模型，结果可能不适用于所有类型的实体瘤，尤其是免疫排斥型（冷）肿瘤。","虽然强调了 AhR 的作用，但未使用 AhR 缺陷小鼠进行反向验证，因此因果关系推断需谨慎，主要基于相关性及已知文献背景。","再挑战实验显示的免疫记忆需结合近期关于此类实验可靠性的争议进行解读，不能过度推广为绝对的长期免疫保护。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"提供了一种基于工程益生菌的局部免疫治疗策略，证明通过瘤内递送 AhR 激动剂 IAA 可有效重编程肿瘤免疫微环境，增强 T 细胞浸润并抑制肿瘤生长。","limits":"研究仅在两种高免疫原性的结直肠癌小鼠模型中进行，尚未在“冷”肿瘤模型或人类临床数据中验证；主要依赖相关性分析（细胞因子与表型），虽提及 AhR 依赖性但缺乏 AhR 敲除小鼠的直接因果验证实验；未评估与其他免疫检查点抑制剂的联合治疗效果。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"体外培养 EcN^{IAA} 上清液","finding":"EcN^{IAA} 产生约 780 µM 的 IAA，显著高于对照组，并能剂量依赖性激活 AhR 报告细胞，证实 IAA 是主要的 AhR 激动剂。"},{"conditions":"CT26 结肠癌小鼠模型，瘤内注射 EcN^{IAA}","finding":"显著降低肿瘤体积，提高生存率；肿瘤内 CD4+ 和 CD8+ T 细胞比例显著增加，FOXP3+ Treg 比例不变，提示免疫抑制微环境改善。"},{"conditions":"MC38 结肠癌小鼠模型，瘤内注射 EcN^{IAA}","finding":"同样显著抑制肿瘤生长并延长生存；清除肿瘤的经治疗小鼠在再次接种 MC38 细胞后未复发，显示产生了持久的免疫记忆。"},{"conditions":"治疗后肿瘤组织及血浆分析","finding":"肿瘤内 IAA 水平升高，AhR 激活增强；促炎趋化因子 CXCL9 和 IFN-γ 显著上调，致瘤性细胞因子 IL-17A 显著下调；血浆中 CXCL11 也升高。"}],"problem_or_question":"如何利用微生物代谢产物（特别是 AhR 配体）来增强实体瘤内的抗肿瘤免疫反应，并开发一种安全有效的微生物疗法以克服现有免疫治疗的局限性？","research_scope":"本研究使用工程化大肠杆菌 Nissle 1917 (EcN) 作为载体，在小鼠结直肠癌同系移植模型（CT26 和 MC38）中，通过瘤内注射局部递送吲哚-3-乙酸 (IAA)，研究其对肿瘤微环境免疫调节及抗肿瘤疗效的影响。"}

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"该论文为综述，重点阐述了肠道菌群失调如何通过影响抗肿瘤免疫反应介导ICIs获得性耐药，并介绍了调节菌群（如益生菌、FMT）作为克服耐药的策略。虽然涉及多种肿瘤类型，但其关于菌群机制的描述具有通用性，可为回答“肠道菌群如何调节ICI疗效及其机制”提供背景信息和具体实例。","scope_interpretation_cautions":["该论文为综述，其关于肠道菌群机制的描述多为汇总现有文献，而非原创性机制研究。","文中提到的菌群与疗效的关联在不同肿瘤类型中可能存在差异，需谨慎外推至所有固体瘤。","部分关于菌群调节疗效的数据来自早期临床试验或临床前模型，临床获益的确切程度和普遍性尚待进一步验证。","抗生素使用与耐药的关系主要是观察性关联，需注意混杂因素。"]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"系统性地归纳了ICIs获得性耐药的多种机制，将其划分为内在和外在因素，并建立了机制与潜在治疗策略之间的对应关系。","limits":"作为综述，其结论依赖于所引用的文献，未进行新的实验验证。部分机制（如肠道菌群的具体作用）仍处于探索阶段，因果关系尚未完全确立。文章未提供具体的荟萃分析数据或统一的耐药评估标准。"}],"key_findings":[{"conditions":"肿瘤细胞内在因素","finding":"获得性耐药可能与新抗原表达的丢失（通过克隆选择或染色体缺失）、MHC-I类分子呈递缺陷（如β2M基因突变或缺失）以及IFN-γ/JAK信号通路突变有关，这些变化导致肿瘤细胞无法被T细胞有效识别或响应免疫攻击。"},{"conditions":"肿瘤细胞外在因素：替代检查点与微环境","finding":"耐药过程中常伴随TIM-3、LAG-3、VISTA、TIGIT等替代抑制性检查点的上调，以及调节性T细胞（Tregs）、髓系衍生抑制细胞（MDSCs）、肿瘤相关巨噬细胞（TAMs）和癌症相关成纤维细胞（CAFs）等免疫抑制细胞的浸润，它们通过分泌抑制性细胞因子（如TGF-β, IL-10）和代谢产物（如腺苷、IDO）构建免疫抑制性肿瘤微环境。"},{"conditions":"表观遗传修饰","finding":"表观遗传改变（如DNA甲基化、组蛋白修饰）可导致T细胞耗竭状态的稳定，使再激活的耗竭T细胞难以转化为记忆T细胞，从而限制长期免疫保护；同时可沉默趋化因子基因，减少T细胞向肿瘤的浸润。"},{"conditions":"肠道菌群失调","finding":"肠道菌群的组成影响ICI疗效。特定有益菌（如Faecalibacterium, Ruminococcaceae, Bifidobacterium）的存在与更好的抗原呈递和T细胞功能相关，而抗生素使用导致的菌群失调或与耐药不良预后相关。粪菌移植（FMT）和特定益生菌可能在某些情况下恢复ICI疗效。"}],"problem_or_question":"尽管ICIs在多种恶性肿瘤中显示出持久的临床疗效，但许多患者在初始响应后会出现获得性耐药，导致疾病进展。目前对于获得性耐药的具体机制尚不明确，且缺乏有效的预测生物标志物和治疗方法。本研究旨在阐明获得性耐药的潜在机制，并为开发克服耐药的新策略提供理论依据。","research_scope":"癌症免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）治疗中获得的耐药性机制及潜在逆转策略，涵盖肿瘤细胞内在因素、微环境外在因素、表观遗传修饰及肠道菌群失调。"}

For the user's review on solid tumors and ICIs, this paper offers valuable background on the general principles of microbiome-immune interaction, identifies key microbial taxa and metabolites associated with ICI response, and discusses the mechanisms (SCFAs, MAMPs, cytokines) through which these effects occur. Findings should not be assumed to be uniform across all solid tumors or ICI types.","Many mechanistic insights are from preclinical mouse models; direct applicability to human solid tumors requires verification.","Clinical associations are often correlative; causality is not always established in human studies.","The review is a narrative synthesis and does not provide quantitative effect sizes or meta-analytic conclusions."]}

Specific microbial components like flagellin (via TLR5) and SCFAs (via GPR43) act as endogenous adjuvants or enhance exogenous adjuvant activity. Dysbiosis in infants and the elderly is linked to poorer vaccine responses."},{"conditions":"Mechanistic investigations across both ICI and vaccine contexts","finding":"Three key factors mediate microbial immunomodulation: 1) Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) which can have context-dependent effects (promoting DC maturation in vaccines but potentially inhibiting it in ICI); 2) MAMPs (e.g., flagellin, peptidoglycan) which stimulate pattern recognition receptors (TLRs, NOD2) on APCs to prime immune responses; 3) Inflammatory cytokines (IL-12, IFN-gamma, IL-10) whose steady-state levels are shaped by the microbiome and influence systemic immunity."}],"problem_or_question":"The review aims to address the heterogeneity in treatment success for immune-targeted interventions (ICIs and vaccines). It seeks to understand the role of the microbiome in determining these outcomes, identify key mechanisms of microbial immunomodulation, and explore how manipulating the microbiome could predict or improve therapeutic responses.","research_scope":"The review focuses on the interaction between the commensal microbiome and the host immune system, specifically examining how this interaction modulates the efficacy of two major classes of immune-targeted interventions: cancer immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and vaccines. It covers clinical observations in human patients (primarily melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, urothelial carcinoma for ICIs; various infectious disease vaccines for vaccination) and preclinical findings from mouse, pig, and chicken models."}

identity.title: Targeting the gut microbiota to enhance the antitumor efficacy and attenuate the toxicity of CAR-T cell therapy: a new hope?

source_supplied_locators.source_excerpt: {"planning_summary":"This review provides a comprehensive overview of how the gut microbiome influences CAR-T cell therapy, serving as a bridge between microbiome research and adoptive cell therapy. It offers specific examples of bacterial taxa associated with response/toxicity and discusses modulation strategies. While it does not directly address Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs) in solid tumors as its primary focus, it provides relevant mechanistic parallels (e.g., T-cell activation, metabolic remodeling) and methodological context (microbiome profiling, FMT applications) that can inform the broader review's understanding of microbiome-immunotherapy interactions.","scope_interpretation_cautions":["The paper primarily reviews CAR-T therapy, not ICIs. Do not assume all findings apply directly to ICIs without noting the modality difference.","Many key findings are from mouse models or small human cohorts; causal claims should be treated as hypotheses.","The review notes conflicting results (e.g., vancomycin vs. broad-spectrum antibiotics), indicating complexity in microbiome-drug interactions.","Solid tumor efficacy data for CAR-T is noted as disappointing in the introduction, so do not extrapolate high efficacy to solid tumors based on this review."]}

{"contribution_and_limits":[{"contribution":"Synthesizes emerging evidence linking gut microbiota composition to CAR-T cell therapy outcomes (efficacy and toxicity), providing a framework for understanding microbiome-immune interactions in adoptive cell therapy.","limits":"The review is narrative and relies on heterogeneous data from different studies with varying methodologies.
